171. def make_sampler(length: int,
172.                  rng: Any,
173.                  algorithm: str,
174.                  split: str,
175.                  batch_size: int,
176.                  multiplier: int,
177.                  randomize_pos: bool,
178.                  enforce_pred_as_input: bool,
179.                  enforce_permutations: bool,
180.                  chunked: bool,
181.                  chunk_length: int,
182.                  sampler_kwargs: Dict[str, Any]):
183.   """Create a sampler with given options.
184. 
185.   Args:
186.     length: Size of samples (i.e., number of nodes in the graph).
187.       A length of -1 will mean that the benchmark
188.       dataset (for the given split) is used. Positive sizes will instantiate
189.       samplers of the corresponding size.
190.     rng: Numpy random state.
191.     algorithm: The name of the algorithm to sample from.
192.     split: 'train', 'val' or 'test'.
193.     batch_size: Samples per batch.
194.     multiplier: Integer multiplier for the number of samples in the dataset,
195.       only used for positive sizes. Negative multiplier means infinite samples.
196.     randomize_pos: Whether to randomize the `pos` input.
197.     enforce_pred_as_input: Whether to convert fixed pred_h hints to inputs.
198.     enforce_permutations: Whether to enforce permutation pointers.
199.     chunked: Whether to chunk the dataset.
200.     chunk_length: Unroll length of chunks, if `chunked` is True.
201.     sampler_kwargs: Extra args passed to the sampler.
202.   Returns:
203.     A sampler (iterator), the number of samples in the iterator (negative
204.     if infinite samples), and the spec.
205.   """
206.   if length < 0:  # load from file
207.     dataset_folder = _maybe_download_dataset(FLAGS.dataset_path)
208.     sampler, num_samples, spec = clrs.create_dataset(folder=dataset_folder,
209.                                                      algorithm=algorithm,
210.                                                      batch_size=batch_size,
211.                                                      split=split)
212.     sampler = sampler.as_numpy_iterator()
213.   else:
214.     num_samples = clrs.CLRS30[split]['num_samples'] * multiplier
215.     sampler, spec = clrs.build_sampler(
216.         algorithm,
217.         seed=rng.randint(2**32),
218.         num_samples=num_samples,
219.         length=length,
220.         **sampler_kwargs,
221.         )
222.     sampler = _iterate_sampler(sampler, batch_size)
223. 
224.   if randomize_pos:
225.     sampler = clrs.process_random_pos(sampler, rng)
226.   if enforce_pred_as_input and algorithm in PRED_AS_INPUT_ALGOS:
227.     spec, sampler = clrs.process_pred_as_input(spec, sampler)
228.   spec, sampler = clrs.process_permutations(spec, sampler, enforce_permutations)
229.   if chunked:
230.     sampler = clrs.chunkify(sampler, chunk_length)
231.   return sampler, num_samples, spec
232. 
233. 
234. def make_multi_sampler(sizes, rng, **kwargs):
235.   """Create a sampler with cycling sample sizes."""
236.   ss = []
237.   tot_samples = 0
238.   for length in sizes:
239.     sampler, num_samples, spec = make_sampler(length, rng, **kwargs)
240.     ss.append(sampler)
241.     tot_samples += num_samples
242. 
243.   def cycle_samplers():
244.     while True:
245.       for s in ss:
246.         yield next(s)
247.   return cycle_samplers(), tot_samples, spec
248. 
249. 
250. def _concat(dps, axis):
251.   return jax.tree_util.tree_map(lambda *x: np.concatenate(x, axis), *dps)
252. 
253. 
254. def collect_and_eval(sampler, predict_fn, sample_count, rng_key, extras):
255.   """Collect batches of output and hint preds and evaluate them."""
256.   processed_samples = 0
257.   preds = []
258.   outputs = []
259.   while processed_samples < sample_count:
260.     feedback = next(sampler)
261.     batch_size = feedback.outputs[0].data.shape[0]
262.     outputs.append(feedback.outputs)
263.     print('mod-run.py, feedback.outputs: ', feedback.outputs)
264.     new_rng_key, rng_key = jax.random.split(rng_key)
265.     cur_preds, _ = predict_fn(new_rng_key, feedback.features)
266.     print('mod-run.py, cur_preds: ', cur_preds["pi"].data)
267.     preds.append(cur_preds)
268.     processed_samples += batch_size
269.   outputs = _concat(outputs, axis=0)
270.   preds = _concat(preds, axis=0)
271.   out = clrs.evaluate(outputs, preds)
272.   if extras:
273.     out.update(extras)
274.   return {k: unpack(v) for k, v in out.items()}
275.

278.   """Create all the samplers."""
279.   train_samplers = []

282.   test_samplers = []
283.   test_sample_counts = []
284.   spec_list = []

302.       logging.info('Creating samplers for algo %s', algorithm)
303. 
304.       p = tuple([0.1 + 0.1 * i for i in range(9)])
305.       if p and algorithm in ['articulation_points', 'bridges',
306.                              'mst_kruskal', 'bipartite_matching']:
307.         # Choose a lower connection probability for the above algorithms,
308.         # otherwise trajectories are very long
309.         p = tuple(np.array(p) / 2)
310.       length_needle = FLAGS.length_needle
311.       sampler_kwargs = dict(p=p, length_needle=length_needle)
312.       if length_needle == 0:
313.         sampler_kwargs.pop('length_needle')
314. 
315.       common_sampler_args = dict(
316.           algorithm=FLAGS.algorithms[algo_idx],
317.           rng=rng,
318.           enforce_pred_as_input=FLAGS.enforce_pred_as_input,
319.           enforce_permutations=FLAGS.enforce_permutations,
320.           chunk_length=FLAGS.chunk_length,

186. def _maybe_download_dataset(dataset_path):
187.   """Download CLRS30 dataset if needed."""
188.   dataset_folder = os.path.join(dataset_path, clrs.get_clrs_folder())
189.   if os.path.isdir(dataset_folder):
190.     logging.info('Dataset found at %s. Skipping download.', dataset_folder)
191.     return dataset_folder
192.   logging.info('Dataset not found in %s. Downloading...', dataset_folder)
193. 
194.   clrs_url = clrs.get_dataset_gcp_url()
195.   request = requests.get(clrs_url, allow_redirects=True)
196.   clrs_file = os.path.join(dataset_path, os.path.basename(clrs_url))
197.   os.makedirs(dataset_folder)
198.   open(clrs_file, 'wb').write(request.content)
199.   shutil.unpack_archive(clrs_file, extract_dir=dataset_folder)
200.   os.remove(clrs_file)
201.   return dataset_folder

204. def make_sampler(length: int,
205.                  rng: Any,
206.                  algorithm: str,
207.                  split: str,
208.                  batch_size: int,
209.                  multiplier: int,
210.                  randomize_pos: bool,
211.                  enforce_pred_as_input: bool,
212.                  enforce_permutations: bool,
213.                  chunked: bool,
214.                  chunk_length: int,
215.                  sampler_kwargs: Dict[str, Any]):
216.   """Create a sampler with given options.
217. 
218.   Args:
219.     length: Size of samples (i.e., number of nodes in the graph).
220.       A length of -1 will mean that the benchmark
221.       dataset (for the given split) is used. Positive sizes will instantiate
222.       samplers of the corresponding size.
223.     rng: Numpy random state.
224.     algorithm: The name of the algorithm to sample from.
225.     split: 'train', 'val' or 'test'.
226.     batch_size: Samples per batch.
227.     multiplier: Integer multiplier for the number of samples in the dataset,
228.       only used for positive sizes. Negative multiplier means infinite samples.
229.     randomize_pos: Whether to randomize the `pos` input.
230.     enforce_pred_as_input: Whether to convert fixed pred_h hints to inputs.
231.     enforce_permutations: Whether to enforce permutation pointers.
232.     chunked: Whether to chunk the dataset.
233.     chunk_length: Unroll length of chunks, if `chunked` is True.
234.     sampler_kwargs: Extra args passed to the sampler.
235.   Returns:
236.     A sampler (iterator), the number of samples in the iterator (negative
237.     if infinite samples), and the spec.
238.   """
239.   if length < 0:  # load from file
240.     #print('run.py loading from dataset')
241.     dataset_folder = _maybe_download_dataset(FLAGS.dataset_path)
242.     sampler, num_samples, spec = clrs.create_dataset(folder=dataset_folder,
243.                                                      algorithm=algorithm,
244.                                                      batch_size=batch_size,
245.                                                      split=split)
246.     sampler = sampler.as_numpy_iterator()
247.   else:
248.     num_samples = clrs.CLRS30[split]['num_samples'] * multiplier
249.     sampler, spec = clrs.build_sampler(
250.         algorithm,
251.         seed=rng.randint(2**32),
252.         num_samples=num_samples,
253.         length=length,
254.         **sampler_kwargs,
255.         )
256.     sampler = _iterate_sampler(sampler, batch_size)
257. 
258.   if randomize_pos:
259.     sampler = clrs.process_random_pos(sampler, rng)
260.   if enforce_pred_as_input and algorithm in PRED_AS_INPUT_ALGOS:
261.     spec, sampler = clrs.process_pred_as_input(spec, sampler)
262.   spec, sampler = clrs.process_permutations(spec, sampler, enforce_permutations)
263.   if chunked:
264.     sampler = clrs.chunkify(sampler, chunk_length)
265.   return sampler, num_samples, spec
266. 
267. 
268. def make_multi_sampler(sizes, rng, **kwargs):
269.   """Create a sampler with cycling sample sizes."""
270.   ss = []
271.   tot_samples = 0
272.   for length in sizes:
273.     sampler, num_samples, spec = make_sampler(length, rng, **kwargs)
274.     ss.append(sampler)
275.     tot_samples += num_samples
276. 
277.   def cycle_samplers():
278.     while True:
279.       for s in ss:
280.         yield next(s)
281.   return cycle_samplers(), tot_samples, spec
282.

284. def _concat(dps, axis):
285.   return jax.tree_util.tree_map(lambda *x: np.concatenate(x, axis), *dps)
286. 
287. 
288. def collect_and_eval(sampler, predict_fn, sample_count, rng_key, extras):
289.   """Collect batches of output and hint preds and evaluate them."""
290.   processed_samples = 0
291.   preds = []
292.   outputs = []
293.   while processed_samples < sample_count:
294.     feedback = next(sampler)
295.     batch_size = feedback.outputs[0].data.shape[0]
296.     outputs.append(feedback.outputs)
297.     new_rng_key, rng_key = jax.random.split(rng_key)
298.     cur_preds, _ = predict_fn(new_rng_key, feedback.features)
299.     preds.append(cur_preds)
300.     processed_samples += batch_size
301.   outputs = _concat(outputs, axis=0)
302.   preds = _concat(preds, axis=0)
303.   out = clrs.evaluate(outputs, preds)
304.   #breakpoint()
305.   if extras:
306.     out.update(extras)
307.   return {k: unpack(v) for k, v in out.items()}
308.

7. ## **SECTION A: Repository Architecture Summary**
8. 
9. ### Overall Structure
10. **Root-level project**: Neural Algorithmic Reasoning framework extended to handle **multiple correct solutions** for underdetermined algorithms (DFS, BFS, Bellman-Ford). Built on DeepMind's CLRS-30 benchmark baseline.
11. 
12. **Directory Layout**:
13. - `/clrs/_src/` — Core algorithmic reasoning source (BASE + CUSTOM)
14.   - `algorithms/` — Algorithm implementations (DFS, BFS, etc.) with multi-solution variants
15.   - `samplers.py` — Dataset generation & algorithm selection (710+ lines; contains DfsMultiSampler, BfsMultiSampler)
16.   - `baselines.py` — GNN baseline models (JAX/Haiku; 799 lines)
17.   - `processors.py` — Graph neural network architectures (914 lines)
18.   - `nets.py` — Model layer definitions (719 lines)
19.   - `model.py` — Abstract Model API
20.   - `encoders.py`, `decoders.py` — Input/output encoding layers
21.   - `losses.py` — Training objectives (including **KL divergence for distribution learning**)
22.   - `probing.py` — Trajectory recording/debugging infrastructure
23.   - `specs.py` — Algorithm I/O specifications (570 lines; includes dfs_multi, bfs_multi, bellman_ford_multi)
24.   - `evaluation.py` — Baseline metrics computation
25.   - **CUSTOM MULTI-SOLUTION FILES**:
26.     - `dfs_sampling.py` — **Stochastic solution extraction** (247 lines): sample_upwards, sample_altUpwards, sample_random_list, sample_argmax
27.     - `bfs_sampling.py` — **BFS tree sampling** (226 lines): sample_bfs_prim, sample_bfs_categorical, sample_bfs_beam
28.     - `dfs_uniqueness_check.py` — Validity & uniqueness metrics for DFS
29.     - `bf_uniqueness_check.py` — Validity & uniqueness metrics for Bellman-Ford
30.     - `validate_distributions.py` — **Core distribution analysis** (914 lines): empirical solution distribution extraction, edge-reuse analysis
31.     - `test_rerunning_number/` — Experimental utilities for multi-run generation
32. 
33. - `/clrs/examples/` — Training & evaluation pipelines
34.   - `run.py` — **Main training loop** (644 lines); flags: `--NSE` (NumSolutionsExtracted), `--algorithms dfs_multi/bfs_multi`
35.   - `log_experiments.py` — **Evaluation functions** (557 lines):
36.     - `DFS_collect_and_eval()` — DFS multi-solution evaluation
37.     - `BFS_multi_collect_and_eval()` — BFS multi-solution evaluation
38.     - `BF_collect_and_eval()` — Bellman-Ford evaluation
39.   - `mod-run.py` — Alternative training entry point
40.   - `plot.py` — Visualization utilities

42. - `/results/`, `/clrs_env/` — Outputs, environment
43. 
44. ### Key Files Bridging CLRS Baseline → Custom Multi-Solution Logic
45. | Purpose | Baseline Component | Custom Extension |
46. |---------|-------------------|------------------|
47. | **Algorithm Definition** | `algorithms/graphs.py` (e.g., `dfs()`) | `dfs_multi()`, `bfs_multi()` at lines 177, 385 — **Generate 20 solutions per input via random shuffling** |
48. | **Data Sampling** | `samplers.py`: `DfsSampler`, `BfsSampler` | `DfsMultiSampler` (line 425), `BfsMultiSampler` (line 458) — **Pass seed to algorithm for reproducible multi-runs** |
49. | **Training Loss** | `losses.py`: MSE, cross-entropy | Line 84 onwards: **KL divergence** (`kl_div()`) for distribution matching |
50. | **Evaluation** | `clrs.evaluate()` standard metrics | `DFS_collect_and_eval`, `BFS_multi_collect_and_eval` in `log_experiments.py` — **5 sampling methods per algorithm** |
51. | **Solution Extraction** | N/A | `dfs_sampling.py`, `bfs_sampling.py` — **Stochastic sampling from learned probability distributions** |
52. 
53. ---
54. 
55. ## **SECTION B: Current Data Pipeline by Stage**
56. 
57. ### **STAGE 1: SAMPLING / GENERATION**
58. **Files**: `clrs/_src/samplers.py` (lines 425-475), `clrs/_src/algorithms/graphs.py`
59. 
60. **For DFS Multi-Solution** (lines 177–343 in graphs.py):
61. ```
62. Input: Adjacency matrix A, seed
63. → DfsMultiSampler generates: [graph, sub_seed]
64. → dfs_multi(A, seed, deterministic=False):
65.     FOR i in range(NUM_SOLUTIONS=20):
66.         - Initialize probes for timesteps
67.         - Shuffle node adjacency order (line 214): rng.shuffle(shuffled)
68.         - Run DFS with randomized neighbor selection (different valid trees)
69.         - Record pi (parent pointers) for each run
70.     → Average all 20 pi outputs → parent_dist (n×n empirical distribution)
71.     → Return: parent_dist, probeslist[0]
72. ```
73. 
74. **For BFS Multi-Solution** (lines 385–468 in graphs.py):
75. ```
76. Input: Adjacency matrix A, source s, seed
77. → BfsMultiSampler generates: [graph, source_node, sub_seed]
78. → bfs_multi(A, s, seed, deterministic=False):
79.     FOR i in range(NUM_SOLUTIONS=20):
80.         - Initialize reach, pi arrays
81.         - Shuffle order of reached nodes (line 434–435): rng.shuffle(shuffled_sources)
82.         - Claim children in random order (multiple valid parents at same distance)
83.         - Record pi for each solution
84.     → Build adj matrix (1 if i is parent of j in solution, else 0)
85.     → Average: parent_dist = sum(adjs) / 20
86.     → Inject into probes['output']['node']['pi']['data'] = parent_dist
87.     → Return: parent_dist, probeslist[0]
88. ```
89. 
90. **Output Format** (from specs.py):
91. - `outputs[0].data` ← probability matrix (n×n), where element [i,j] = P(j is parent of i)
92. 
93. ### **STAGE 2: DATASET HANDLING & BATCHING**
94. **Files**: `clrs/_src/samplers.py` (lines 65–283), `clrs/examples/run.py` (lines 204–267)
95. 
96. **Sampler Chain**:
97. ```python
98. Sampler._sample_data(length)
99.   ↓ (for multi-solutions)
100.   → DfsMultiSampler._sample_data(length)
101.     → Returns [graph, sub_seed]
102.     → Used by: dfs_multi(graph, sub_seed)
103. 
104. make_sampler() in run.py:
105.   1. build_sampler(name='dfs_multi', seed, num_samples, length)
106.   2. Batch via sampler.next(batch_size)
107.   3. Yields Feedback(features, outputs)
108.      - features.inputs: [pos, A]
109.      - features.outputs: probability matrices
110. 
111. make_multi_sampler(sizes, rng):
112.   → Creates samplers for multiple training sizes simultaneously
113.   → Used in line 268-275 for flexible training
114. ```
115. 
116. **Batching** (Sampler._make_batch, lines 117–179):
117. ```
118. FOR each sample in batch:
119.   - Call _sample_data(length) → gets problem instance
120.   - Run algorithm → get probes
121.   - Pad probes to max_time_length
122.   - Concatenate across batch dimension
123.   → Result: batch of DataPoints with time-padded hints/outputs
124. ```
125. 
126. ### **STAGE 3: MODEL ARCHITECTURE & FORWARD PASS**
127. **Files**: `clrs/_src/baselines.py` (lines 136–496), `clrs/_src/nets.py` (lines 1–719)
128. 
129. **Training Model** (BaselineModel, lines 136–496 in baselines.py):
130. ```
131. Input: features.inputs (graph + positions)
132.   ↓
133. Encoder (encoders.py):
134.   - Embed node positions, edges, graph-level features
135.   - Project to hidden_dim
136.   ↓
137. Processor (processors.py) × T timesteps:
138.   - Graph Neural Network (GAT, MPNN, Deep Sets, etc.)
139.   - Recurrent message passing (nb_msg_passing_steps)
140.   - Attend over hint trajectories
141.   ↓
142. Decoder (decoders.py):
143.   - For each probe in spec (e.g., 'pi'):
144.     - Predict node→node logits or probabilities
145.     - Output shape: [batch, n_nodes, n_nodes] for parent pointers
146.   ↓
147. Output: preds['pi'].data ← **learned probability distribution** over parent assignments
148. ```
149. 
150. **Loss Computation** (losses.py, lines 84–147):
151. ```python
152. For multi-solution outputs:
153.   truth = outputs[0].data  # Empirical distribution (n×n)
154.   pred = model_output      # Predicted distribution (n×n)
155.   
156.   loss = KL_div(truth, pred)  # Line 138
157.        = mean(sum(truth * log(truth / (pred + epsilon))))
158.   
159. Purpose: Match learned distribution to empirical distribution of 20 solutions
160. ```
161. 
162. ### **STAGE 4: TRAINING LOOP**
163. **Files**: `clrs/examples/run.py` (lines 484–576)
164. 
165. ```python
166. WHILE step < train_steps:
167.   1. Get feedback from train_samplers[algo_idx]
168.      → Multi-solution: outputs = empirical distribution
169.   
170.   2. train_model.feedback(rng_key, feedback, algo_idx)
171.      → Compute loss via KL divergence
172.      → Update model params via Adam optimizer
173.      → Gradient clipping (max_norm=1.0)
174.   
175.   3. Every eval_every steps:
176.      → Run validation on val_samplers
177.      → Compute val_score
178.      → Save best checkpoint if improved
179.   
180.   4. Evaluation callbacks:
181.      → If 'dfs_multi': DFS_collect_and_eval()
182.      → If 'bfs_multi': BFS_multi_collect_and_eval()
183.      → If 'bf': BF_collect_and_eval()
184. ```
185. 
186. ### **STAGE 5: SAMPLING / EXTRACTION**
187. **Files**: `clrs/_src/dfs_sampling.py` (247 lines), `clrs/_src/bfs_sampling.py` (226 lines)
188. 
189. **Five DFS Sampling Methods**:
190. 1. **Argmax** (line 6–33): Choose parent with highest probability per node
191. 2. **Random** (line 36–60): Sample parent uniformly from all nodes
192. 3. **Upwards** (line 102–160): Leaf-first greedy with upward tree construction
193. 4. **AltUpwards** (line 213–241): Alternative leaf-first with node traversal
194. 5. (Beam search also available in BF_beamsearch.py)
195. 
196. **Four BFS Sampling Methods**:
197. 1. **Categorical** (line 98–128): Independent parent sampling per node (may create cycles)
198. 2. **Prim-like** (line 4–27, 29–96): Greedy MST-style: add nodes with highest probability to process set
199. 3. **Beam Search** (line 130–227): Maintain top-k hypotheses, branch on all possible parents
200. 4. **Argmax** (reused from DFS)
201. 
202. ### **STAGE 6: VALIDATION & EVALUATION**
203. **Files**: `clrs/examples/log_experiments.py` (557 lines), `clrs/_src/dfs_uniqueness_check.py`, `clrs/_src/bf_uniqueness_check.py`
204. 
205. **DFS Evaluation** (DFS_collect_and_eval, lines 382–550):
206. ```
207. FOR EACH sampling method (random, argmax, upwards, altupwards):
208.   1. Sample K solutions from learned model distribution
209.   2. Sample K solutions from ground-truth distribution
210.   
211.   3. Check validity: dfs_verification_tester.dfsverify(A, tree)
212.      → Verify tree structure constraints
213.   
214.   4. Compute uniqueness (check_uniqueness_dfs):
215.      - Run 5 samples each
216.      - Count unique valid solutions
217.      - Compute fraction valid
218.   
219.   5. Log: accuracy per sampling method (model vs truth)
220.          uniqueness metrics
221.          validity metrics
222.   
223. Output: CSV results with 15+ metrics per method
224. ```
225. 
226. **BFS Evaluation** (BFS_multi_collect_and_eval, lines 242–375):
227. ```
228. FOR EACH sampling method (categorical, prim, beam, argmax):
229.   1. Sample from model & ground-truth distributions
230.   2. Validate: check_graphs.check_valid_bfsTree(A, tree, s)
231.   3. Log accuracy per method
232.   4. Compare model vs truth correctness
233. ```
234. 
235. **Distribution Validation** (validate_distributions.py, 914 lines):
236. ```
237. validate_distributions(As, Ss, outsOrPreds, numSolsExtracting=NSE):
238.   → Extract numSolsExtracting solutions from model
239.   → For each solution: record edge usage
240.   → Compute edge-reuse matrix (how many times each edge appears)
241.   → Generate plots: distribution of unique solutions vs extraction count
242.   → Assess solution diversity
243. ```
244. 
245. ---
246. 
247. ## **SECTION C: BFS-Specific vs DFS-Specific Multi-Solution Code Paths**
248. 
249. ### **DFS (Underdetermined via Random Shuffling)**
250. | Component | Location | Detail |
251. |-----------|----------|--------|
252. | **Algorithm** | `graphs.py:177–343` | `dfs_multi()`: Shuffle adjacency ordering per run; all orderings valid |
253. | **Sampler** | `samplers.py:425–440` | `DfsMultiSampler`: Provides seed to algorithm |
254. | **Specs** | `specs.py:295` | `'dfs_multi'`: Input=[pos, A]; Output=pi (n×n distribution) |
255. | **Extraction** | `dfs_sampling.py` lines 102–241 | **5 methods**: argmax, random, upwards, altupwards, (+ beam in BF module) |
256. | **Validation** | `dfs_uniqueness_check.py` | `check_uniqueness_dfs()`: Upwards & AltUpwards sampling; validity check |
257. | **Eval** | `log_experiments.py:382–550` | `DFS_collect_and_eval()`: Runs 5 methods, computes uniqueness & validity |
258. 
259. ### **BFS (Underdetermined via Random Parent Selection at Same Distance)**
260. | Component | Location | Detail |

```
1. import numpy as np
2. from clrs._src import dfs_sampling

4. def sample_bfs_prim(outsOrPreds, s_indices):
5.     """
6.     Samples BFS trees using a Prim-like greedy approach.
7.     
8.     Args:
9.         outsOrPreds: Model outputs containing parent probabilities.
10.         s_indices: List of source node indices for each graph in the batch.
11.         
12.     Returns:
13.         List of parent arrays (pi), one for each graph in the batch.
14.     """
15.     probMatrix_list = dfs_sampling.extract_probMatrices(outsOrPreds)
16.     pi_trees = []
17.     
18.     # Handle case where s_indices might be a single int or list
19.     if isinstance(s_indices, int):
20.         s_indices = [s_indices] * len(probMatrix_list)
21.         
22.     for i, probMatrix in enumerate(probMatrix_list):
23.         s = s_indices[i]
24.         pi = prim_like_sampler(probMatrix, s)
25.         pi_trees.append(pi)
26.         
27.     return pi_trees
28. 
29. def prim_like_sampler(probMatrix, s):
30.     """
31.     Constructs a BFS tree starting from the root, adding nodes that are most likely 
32.     connected to the current tree.
33.     
34.     Args:
35.         probMatrix: N x N matrix where P[i, j] is prob that j is parent of i.
36.         s: Source node index.
37.         
38.     Returns:
39.         pi: Array of length N, where pi[i] is the parent of i.
40.     """
41.     num_nodes = probMatrix.shape[0]
42.     pi = np.full(num_nodes, -1, dtype=int) # -1 indicates not yet processed/no parent
43.     pi[s] = s
44.     
45.     processed = {s}
46.     remaining = set(range(num_nodes)) - {s}
47.     
48.     # To optimize, we could maintain scores, but N is likely small (<= 64 usually in CLRS)
49.     # So recomputing sum might be fast enough.
50.     
51.     while remaining:
52.         best_v = -1
53.         best_score = -1.0
54.         
55.         # Find v in remaining with highest prob of attaching to processed set
56.         # score(v) = sum_{u in processed} P(parent(v) = u)
57.         for v in remaining:
58.             # probMatrix[v, u] is prob that u is parent of v.
59.             # We sum over u in processed.
60.             score = sum(probMatrix[v, u] for u in processed)
61.             
62.             if score > best_score:
63.                 best_score = score
64.                 best_v = v
65.         
66.         if best_v == -1:
67.             # This happens if remaining nodes have 0 prob of connecting to processed nodes
68.             # (disconnected graph components). 
69.             # We just pick one arbitrarily or handle it?
70.             # For BFS, disconnected nodes typically point to themselves or have 0 parent in some representations.
71.             # Here, let's just pick the first one and attach it to itself (or closest processed if any non-zero).
72.             best_v = list(remaining)[0]
73.             # If score is 0, it means no connection.
74.             # We'll just process it to avoid infinite loop.
75.             
76.         # Sample parent for best_v from processed set
77.         # Probabilities are P(parent(best_v) = u) for u in processed
78.         # We need to normalize these to sum to 1.
79.         
80.         candidate_parents = list(processed)
81.         probs = np.array([probMatrix[best_v, u] for u in candidate_parents])
82.         
83.         total_prob = probs.sum()
84.         if total_prob > 0:
85.             probs = probs / total_prob
86.             parent = np.random.choice(candidate_parents, p=probs)
87.         else:
88.             # No valid parent in processed set (disconnected). 
89.             # Default to self-loop or some fallback.
90.             parent = best_v 
91.             
92.         pi[best_v] = parent
93.         processed.add(best_v)
94.         remaining.remove(best_v)
95.         
96.     return pi
97. 
98. def sample_bfs_categorical(outsOrPreds):
99.     """
100.     Samples parent pointers independently for each node using categorical sampling.
101.     Note: This does NOT guarantee a tree structure (may contain cycles or orphans).
102.     
103.     Args:           
104.         outsOrPreds: Model outputs containing parent probabilities.
105.         
106.     Returns:
107.         List of parent arrays (pi).
108.     """
109.     probMatrix_list = dfs_sampling.extract_probMatrices(outsOrPreds)
110.     pi_trees = []
111.     
112.     for probMatrix in probMatrix_list:
113.         num_nodes = probMatrix.shape[0]
114.         pi = np.zeros(num_nodes, dtype=int)
115.         
116.         for i in range(num_nodes):
117.             # Sample parent for node i based on the distribution in row i
118.             probs = probMatrix[i]
119.             # Ensure probabilities sum to 1 for np.random.choice
120.             total_p = np.sum(probs)
121.             assert total_p >= 0, "Probabilities must be non-negative"
122.             if total_p > 0:
123.                 normalized_probs = probs / total_p
124.                 pi[i] = np.random.choice(num_nodes, p=normalized_probs)
125.                 
126.         pi_trees.append(pi)
127.         
128.     return pi_trees

130. def sample_bfs_beam(outsOrPreds, s_indices, beam_width=3):
131.     """
132.     Samples BFS trees using a Beam Search approach.
133.     
134.     Args:
135.         outsOrPreds: Model outputs containing parent probabilities.
136.         s_indices: List of source node indices.
137.         beam_width: Number of hypotheses to keep.
138.         
139.     Returns:
140.         List of parent arrays (pi).
141.     """
142.     probMatrix_list = dfs_sampling.extract_probMatrices(outsOrPreds)
143.     pi_trees = []
144.     
145.     if isinstance(s_indices, int):
146.         s_indices = [s_indices] * len(probMatrix_list)
147.         
148.     for i, probMatrix in enumerate(probMatrix_list):
149.         s = s_indices[i]
150.         pi = bfs_beam_sampler(probMatrix, s, beam_width)
151.         pi_trees.append(pi)
152.         
153.     return pi_trees
154. 
155. def bfs_beam_sampler(probMatrix, s, beam_width):
156.     num_nodes = probMatrix.shape[0]
157.     
158.     # State: (log_prob, pi_array, processed_set_as_tuple)
159.     # processed_set is stored as tuple for hashing/copying if needed, though sets are fine if we copy.
160.     # pi_array initialized with -1
161.     initial_pi = np.full(num_nodes, -1, dtype=int)
162.     initial_pi[s] = s
163.     
164.     # Beam: list of dicts or objects. 
165.     # Let's use a simple dict: {'log_prob': 0.0, 'pi': pi, 'processed': {s}}
166.     beam = [{'log_prob': 0.0, 'pi': initial_pi, 'processed': {s}}]
167.     
168.     # We need to add N-1 nodes
169.     for _ in range(num_nodes - 1):
170.         candidates = []
171.         
172.         for hyp in beam:
173.             processed = hyp['processed']
174.             pi = hyp['pi']
175.             curr_log_prob = hyp['log_prob']
176.             remaining = set(range(num_nodes)) - processed
177.             
178.             if not remaining:
179.                 candidates.append(hyp)
180.                 continue
181.             
182.             # 1. Select next node `v` to add (Greedy heuristic)
183.             # We pick the v with highest total probability of connecting to current processed set
184.             best_v = -1
185.             best_connection_mass = -1.0
186.             
187.             for v in remaining:
188.                 # Sum of probs from processed nodes to v
189.                 # probMatrix[v, u] is P(parent(v)=u)
190.                 mass = sum(probMatrix[v, u] for u in processed)
191.                 if mass > best_connection_mass:
192.                     best_connection_mass = mass
193.                     best_v = v
194.             
195.             if best_v == -1:
196.                 best_v = list(remaining)[0] # Disconnected/fallback
197.                 
198.             # 2. Branch on all possible parents u in processed for best_v
199.             possible_parents = list(processed)
200.             
201.             for u in possible_parents:
202.                 p_val = probMatrix[best_v, u]
203.                 if p_val > 1e-9: # Avoid log(0)
204.                     new_log_prob = curr_log_prob + np.log(p_val)
205.                 else:
206.                     new_log_prob = curr_log_prob - 1e9 # Penalty
207.                 
208.                 new_pi = pi.copy()
209.                 new_pi[best_v] = u
210.                 new_processed = processed.copy()
211.                 new_processed.add(best_v)
212.                 
213.                 candidates.append({
214.                     'log_prob': new_log_prob,
215.                     'pi': new_pi,
216.                     'processed': new_processed
217.                 })
218.         
219.         if not candidates:
220.             break # Should not happen usually unless disconnected
221. 
222.         # Select top-k candidates
223.         # Sort by log_prob descending
224.         candidates.sort(key=lambda x: x['log_prob'], reverse=True)
225.         beam = candidates[:beam_width]
226.         
227.     return beam[0]['pi'] # Return best hypothesis
```

```
162. def leafinessSort(probMatrix):
163.     '''
164.     Args:
165.         probMatrix: Expects probMatrix[i][j] to indicate the probability that node j is the parent of node i
166. 
167.     Returns: sorted-list of vertex indices where first node had lowest probability of being parent. (column with lowest sum).
168.     '''
169.     sums = np.sum(probMatrix, axis=0)
170.     # sort by sum column, remember the original column number
171.     leafiness = np.argsort(sums)
172.     return leafiness
173. 
174. def rowWiseProb(probMatrix):
175.     for row_ix in range(len(probMatrix)):
176.         if probMatrix[row_ix].sum() != 0:
177.             probMatrix[row_ix] = probMatrix[row_ix].astype(np.float64)/probMatrix[row_ix].astype(np.float64).sum()
178.     return probMatrix

201. def chooseUniformly(notProbArray):
202.     '''Expects notProbArray'''
203.     val = np.random.uniform(low=0, high=sum(notProbArray))
204.     sums = np.cumsum(notProbArray)
205.     for threshold_ix in range(len(sums)):
206.         if val < sums[threshold_ix]:
207.             return threshold_ix
208.     return np.random.randint(len(notProbArray))

222. def get_parent_tree_upwards(probMatrix):
223.     '''according to leafiness, explore upwards, until all nodes have parents (could be themselves)'''
224.     parent_guesses = np.full(len(probMatrix), np.inf)
225.     leafiness = leafinessSort(probMatrix)  # most leafy is least-likely to be a parent: lowest column sum of probMatrix
226.     for node_ix in leafiness:
227.         if parent_guesses[node_ix] == np.inf:
228.             parent_guesses = explore_upwards(node_ix, parent_guesses, probMatrix)
229.     if np.inf in parent_guesses:
230.         raise ValueError('not guessing parent for someone')
231.     return parent_guesses
232. 
233. def explore_upwards(orphan_ix, parent_guesses, probMatrix):
234.     '''starting at node_ix, sample parents upwards until you find a node which already has a parent'''
235.     while parent_guesses[orphan_ix] == np.inf: # until you find node who already has parent,
236.         # sample parent according to row of notExactlyProbs
237.         parent_guess = chooseUniformly(probMatrix[orphan_ix])
238.         parent_guesses[orphan_ix] = parent_guess
239.         # try further up the tree
240.         orphan_ix = parent_guess
241.     return parent_guesses
```

```
341. def bfs(A: _Array, s: int) -> _Out:
342.   """Breadth-first search (Moore, 1959)."""
343.

354.           's': probing.mask_one(s, A.shape[0]),
355.           'A': np.copy(A),
356.           'adj': probing.graph(np.copy(A))
357.       })

364.     probing.push(
365.         probes,
366.         specs.Stage.HINT,

370.         })
371.     for i in range(A.shape[0]):

375.             pi[j] = i
376.           reach[j] = 1
377.     if np.all(reach == prev_reach):

380.   probing.push(probes, specs.Stage.OUTPUT, next_probe={'pi': np.copy(pi)})
381.   probing.finalize(probes)
382. 
383.   return pi, probes

385. def bfs_multi(A: _Array, s: int, seed: int, deterministic=False) -> _Out:
386.   """Multiple solution breadth-first search."""
387.   rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
388. 
389.   chex.assert_rank(A, 2)
390.   probeslist = []
391.   pies = []
392. 
393.   if deterministic:
394.     NUM_SOLUTIONS = 1
395.   else: 
396.     NUM_SOLUTIONS = 20
397. 
398.   for i in range(NUM_SOLUTIONS):
399.     probes = probing.initialize(specs.SPECS['bfs_multi'])
400. 
401.     A_pos = np.arange(A.shape[0])
402. 
403.     probing.push(
404.         probes,
405.         specs.Stage.INPUT,
406.         next_probe={
407.             'pos': np.copy(A_pos) * 1.0 / A.shape[0],
408.             's': probing.mask_one(s, A.shape[0]),
409.             'A': np.copy(A),
410.             'adj': probing.graph(np.copy(A))
411.         })
412. 
413.     reach = np.zeros(A.shape[0])
414.     pi = np.arange(A.shape[0])
415.     reach[s] = 1
416.     while True:
417.       prev_reach = np.copy(reach)
418.       probing.push(
419.           probes,
420.           specs.Stage.HINT,
421.           next_probe={
422.               'reach_h': np.copy(prev_reach),
423.               'pi_h': np.copy(pi)
424.           })
425.       
426.       # Randomise order of sources (reached nodes) to generate different valid BFS trees
427.       # All nodes in prev_reach are at the same distance from root, so any can be a valid parent
428.       # Shuffling determines which one "claims" a child first when multiple are valid
429.       n = A.shape[0]
430.       sources = np.where(prev_reach == 1)[0]
431.       if deterministic:
432.         shuffled_sources = sources
433.       else:
434.         shuffled_sources = np.copy(sources)
435.         rng.shuffle(shuffled_sources)
436.       for src in shuffled_sources:
437.         for j in range(n):
438.           if A[src, j] > 0:
439.             if pi[j] == j and j != s:
440.               pi[j] = src
441.             reach[j] = 1
442.       if np.all(reach == prev_reach):
443.         break
444. 
445.     probing.push(probes, specs.Stage.OUTPUT, next_probe={'pi': np.copy(pi)})
446.     probing.finalize(probes)
447. 
448.     pies.append(pi)
449.     probeslist.append(probes)
450. 
451.   ### copied from DFS CODE
452.   # build adj matrix of "is i a parent of j in any pi", sums and divides.
453.   adjs = []
454.   for i in range(NUM_SOLUTIONS):
455.       adj = np.zeros(A.shape)
456.       for j in range(len(pies[0])):  # what's the parent of j?
457.           #breakpoint()
458.           adj[j, pies[i][j]] = 1  # at row j, put 1 in the column corresponding to parent
459.       adjs.append(adj)
460.   parent_dist = sum(adjs) / NUM_SOLUTIONS
461.   # parent_dist = sp.special.logit(parent_dist)
462.   # print(probes)
463.   # print(parent_dist)
464.   probeslist[0]['output']['node']['pi']['data'] = parent_dist
465. 
466.   #breakpoint()
467.   ## CHECK THE PUSHING!
468.   return parent_dist, probeslist[0]
469.
```

```
366. class OptimalBSTSampler(Sampler):
367.   """Optimal BST sampler. Samples array of probabilities, splits it into two."""
368. 
369.   def _sample_data(
370.       self,
```

```
23. def parent_tree_to_adj_matrix(tree):
24.     size = len(tree)    # n_vertices
25.     M = np.zeros((size, size))
26.     for ix in range(size):
27.         M[int(tree[ix]), ix] = 1     # edge points tree[ix] to ix, bcuz parent tree
28.     return M
29. 
30. def no_self_loops_parent_tree_to_adj_matrix(tree):
31.     """now root is just any node without parent"""
32.     M = parent_tree_to_adj_matrix(tree)
33.     np.fill_diagonal(a=M, val=0)
34.     return M
35. 
36. def adj_matrix_to_parent_tree(A):
37.     size = len(A)
38.     tree = np.zeros(size)
39.     for i in range(size):
40.         for j in range(size):
41.             if A[i,j] == 1:
42.                 tree[j] = i
43.     return tree

48. # 1. run sampling algorithms increasingly many times on preds
49. # 2. count how many valid unique solutions
50. # 3. count how many invalid unique solutions
51. # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
52. 
53. # solution, beamOrGreedy?, valid?, unique?, how_many_times_found?, (maybe also adjacency matrix)

57. def validate_distributions(As, Ss, outsOrPreds, flag, numSolsExtracting = 100, edge_reuse_BF= False, edge_reuse_DFS = False):
58.     #breakpoint()

60.     dataframes = []

67.         # build a plot,
68.         if flag=='BF':
69.             dataframes.append(make_n_unique_by_n_extracted_df(A=A, s=startNode, pred=probMatrix, num_solutions_extracted=numSolsExtracting))
70.         elif edge_reuse_BF:
71.             matrix_lists = make_edge_reuse_matrix_list(A, startNode, probMatrix,numSolsExtracting)
72.             df = postprocess_edge_reuse_matrix_list(matrix_lists)
73.             dataframes.append(df)
74.         elif flag=='DFS':
75.             df, A, pM = DFS_graph1_df(A=A, pred=probMatrix, num_solutions_extracted=numSolsExtracting)
76.             dataframes.append(df)
77.             pMs.append(pM)
78.         elif edge_reuse_DFS:
79.             matrix_lists = make_edge_reuse_matrix_list_dfs(A, probMatrix, numSolsExtracting)
80.             df = postprocess_edge_reuse_matrix_list_dfs(matrix_lists)
81.             dataframes.append(df)
82.         else:
83.             raise ValueError('no flag given to validate_distributions')
84.     return dataframes, As, pMs

88. def DFS_graph1_df(A, pred, num_solutions_extracted):
89.     # columns for dataframe
90.     upwards_trees = []
91.     upwards_valid = []
92.     upwards_unique = []
93. 
94.     dfs_trees = []
95.     dfs_valid = []
96.     dfs_unique = []
97. 
98.     altUpwards_trees = []
99.     altUpwards_valid = []
100.     altUpwards_unique = []
101. 
102.     # frequency dicts
103.     upwards_dict = dict()
104.     altUpwards_dict = dict()
105.     dfs_dict = dict()
106. 
107.     # core routine
108.     num_sampled = 0
109.     while num_sampled < num_solutions_extracted:
110.         num_sampled += 1
111.         # extract new trees
112.         up_tree = single_sample_upwards(pred)
113.         alt_tree = get_parent_tree_upwards(pred)
114.         dfs_tree = adj_matrix_to_parent_tree(dfs(A, deterministic=True)[0])
115.         # save them for later dataframe
116.         upwards_trees.append(up_tree)
117.         altUpwards_trees.append(alt_tree)
118.         dfs_trees.append(dfs_tree)
119. 
120.         #breakpoint()
121.         # valid?
122.         upwards_valid.append(dfsverify(A, no_self_loops_parent_tree_to_adj_matrix(up_tree)))
123.         altUpwards_valid.append(dfsverify(A, no_self_loops_parent_tree_to_adj_matrix(alt_tree)))
124. 
125.         # unique?
126.         hash_up = hash(tuple(up_tree))
127.         upwards_unique.append(hash_up not in upwards_dict.keys())
128.         hash_alt = hash(tuple(alt_tree))
129.         altUpwards_unique.append(hash_alt not in altUpwards_dict.keys())
130.         hash_dfs = hash(tuple(dfs_tree))
131.         dfs_unique.append(hash_dfs not in dfs_dict.keys())
132. 
133.         # update freq dict
134.         if hash_up not in upwards_dict.keys():
135.             upwards_dict[hash_up] = 1
136.         else:
137.             upwards_dict[hash_up] += 1
138. 
139.         if hash_alt not in altUpwards_dict.keys():
140.             altUpwards_dict[hash_alt] = 1
141.         else:
142.             altUpwards_dict[hash_alt] += 1
143. 
144.         if hash_dfs not in dfs_dict.keys():
145.             dfs_dict[hash_dfs] = 1
146.         else:
147.             dfs_dict[hash_dfs] += 1
148. 
149.     df = pd.DataFrame.from_dict(
150.             {'up_trees': upwards_trees, 'unique_up': upwards_unique, 'valid_up': upwards_valid,
151.              'alt_trees': altUpwards_trees, 'unique_alt': altUpwards_unique, 'valid_alt': altUpwards_valid,
152.              'dfs_trees' : dfs_trees, 'unique_dfs': dfs_unique}
153.     )
154.     df['total_unique_seen'] = df['unique_alt'].cumsum()
155.     df['total_valid_seen'] = df['valid_alt'].cumsum()
156.     df['total_uv_seen_alt'] = (df['unique_alt'] & df['valid_alt']).cumsum()
157.     df['total_uv_seen_upwards'] = (df['unique_up'] & df['valid_up']).cumsum()
158.     df['total_uv_seen_dfs'] = df['unique_dfs'].cumsum()
159. 
160.     return df, A, pred

203. def postprocess_edge_reuse_matrix_list_dfs(matrix_lists):
204.     """
205.     Convert many solutions (matrix_lists) from a single graph & predicted probMatrix, into a df of means by n_sols
206.     Args:
207.         matrix_lists: a list of lists [[alt_list], [upwards_list], [dfs_list]]
208.             each inner list (e.g. [alt_list]) contains adjacency matrices. Each adjacency matrix is a BF path.
209. 
210.     Returns:
211.         df: pandas Dataframe with alt, upwards, and dfs means and medians
212.     """
213.     # this is all for a single graph, where each matrix represents a subset of edges... perhaps in graph... extracted from parent tree
214.     # at each interval, sum adjacency matrices, calculate frequency, report score
215.     # TODO: filter by validity?
216. 
217.     # breakpoint()
218.     # n_samples_list = []
219.     medians = []
220.     means = []
221.     for matrix_list in matrix_lists:
222.         median_list = []
223.         mean_list = []
224.         for ix in range(len(matrix_list)):
225.             # n_samples_list.append(ix+1)
226. 
227.             # sum first how-many np.arrays
228.             summing_list = matrix_list[:ix + 1]
229.             sum_matrix = np.sum(summing_list, axis=0)
230.             frac_matrix = sum_matrix / (ix + 1)
231.             # exclude 0s
232.             frac_matrix = frac_matrix[frac_matrix != 0]
233.             # compute summary stats
234.             median = np.median(frac_matrix)
235.             mean = np.mean(frac_matrix)
236.             # breakpoint()
237. 
238.             # save them
239.             median_list.append(median)
240.             mean_list.append(mean)
241.         medians.append(median_list)
242.         means.append(mean_list)
243. 
244.     # breakpoint()
245.     df = pd.DataFrame.from_dict(
246.         {'alt_medians': medians[0], 'alt_means': means[0],
247.          'upwards_medians': medians[1], 'upwards_means': means[1],
248.          'dfs_medians': medians[2], 'dfs_means': means[2]}
249.     )
250. 
251.     return df
252.

254. def make_edge_reuse_matrix_list_dfs(A, pred, num_solutions_extracted):
255.     """
256.     For a single graph & predicted probMatrix, plot Y-axis: edge reuse by X-axis: num samples
257. 
258.     Args:
259.         A: An adjacency matrix (np.array)
260.         pred: A probability distribution (list of lists, floats in each entry)
261.         num_solutions_extracted: An integer (e.g. 5) indicating the number of solutions to extract from pred
262. 
263.     Returns:
264.         matrices: list of adjacency matrices. Each adjacency matrix is a BF path (i.e. one solution).
265.     """
266.     # gather many solutions
267.     sol_counter = 0
268.     alt_matrices = []
269.     upwards_matrices = []
270.     dfs_matrices = []
271. 
272.     while sol_counter < num_solutions_extracted:
273.         sol_counter += 1
274.         alt_tree = get_parent_tree_upwards(pred)
275.         upwards_tree = single_sample_upwards(pred)
276.         dfs_matrix = dfs(A, deterministic=True)[0]
277. 
278.         # convert tree to adjacency matrix
279.         alt_matrix = parent_tree_to_adj_matrix(alt_tree)
280.         upwards_matrix = parent_tree_to_adj_matrix(upwards_tree)
281. 
282.         # save tree adj matrix
283.         alt_matrices.append(alt_matrix)
284.         upwards_matrices.append(upwards_matrix)
285.         dfs_matrices.append(dfs_matrix)
286.     # breakpoint()
287. 
288.     return [alt_matrices, upwards_matrices, dfs_matrices]
```

```
51. def check_valid_dfsTree_new(A, pi):
52.     '''checks: acyclic, dangling, edge-validity, and valid-start'''
53.     '''
54.         inputs: Adjacency Matrix (A), purported parent forest (pi)
55.         returns: True iff (pi) is producible by run of DFS with random edge exploration but ordered restarts
56.     '''
57.     pi = copy.deepcopy(pi) # copy pi. make sure don't mess with logging
58. 
59.     # build adjacency matrix of DFS forest
60.     size = len(pi)  # n_vertices
61.     M = np.zeros((size, size))
62.     for ix in range(size):
63.         M[int(pi[ix]), ix] = 1
64. 
65.     G = nx.from_numpy_array(A, create_using=nx.DiGraph)
66.     F = nx.from_numpy_array(M, create_using=nx.DiGraph)
67. 
68.     # for each child of node 0 in G, identify all descendants (vertices reachable from child)
69.     # find the children
70. 
71.     children = []   # children of source (node 0)
72.     for i in range(size):
73.         if M[0, i] == 1:
74.             children.append(i)
75. 
76.     descendants_children_G = descendants_children(G, children)
77.     descendants_children_F = descendants_children(F, children)
78. 
79.     while G.number_of_nodes != 0:
80.         changed = False
81.         for child in children:
82.             if descendants_children_G[child] == descendants_children_F[child]:
83.                 # A valid run of DFS can discover all these descendants, then backtrack to source
84.                 # So, remove all these descendants from graph (you don't have to worry about them, this part of forest is ok)
85.                 changed = True
86.                 for desc in descendants_children_G[child]:
87.                     G.remove_node(desc)
88.                     F.remove_node(desc)
89.                     if desc in children:
90.                         children.remove(desc)
91.                 children.remove(child)
92.                 #breakpoint()
93.                 # recompute descendants of first-layer children, with marked-descendants removed
94.                 descendants_children_G = descendants_children(G, children)
95.                 descendants_children_F = descendants_children(F, children)
96.         if not changed:
97.             return False
98.     return True

100. def descendants_children(G, children):
101.     '''
102.     Method to return the descendants of a list of vertices in a nx.DiGraph as a dictionary.
103.     '''
104.     size = G.number_of_nodes()
105.     #breakpoint()
106.     #print('G=',G.nodes())
107.     #print('kids=', children)
108.     #print('size=', size)
109.     descendant_dict = {}
110.     for child in children:
111.         descs = []
112.         for node_id in G.nodes():
113.             if node_id != child:    # cant be self-parent if you're already child of source
114.                 if nx.has_path(G, child, node_id):
115.                     descs.append(node_id)
116.         descendant_dict[child] = descs
117.     return descendant_dict

167. def are_valid_order_parents(np_input_array, pi):
168.     """
169.     Checks whether self-loops stem from valid DFS execution.
170.         If you were reachable_by_earlier_node, but have self-loop, it's a problem
171.     :param input:
172.     :param pi:
173.     :return:
174.     """
175.     g = nx.from_numpy_array(np_input_array, create_using=nx.DiGraph)
176.     for i in range(len(pi)):
177.         if pi[i] == i:
178.             for j in range(i): # crucially, this does not run when i=0, so the starting 0,0 self-loop always permitted
179.                 self_reachable_by_earlier_node = nx.has_path(g, j, i) # does this do it directed? lower-triangle?
180.                 if self_reachable_by_earlier_node:
181.                     return False
182.         else:  # not self-loop, so not a restart, make sure parents are reachable by lowest ix node from which i is reachable
183.             for j in range(i):
184.                 if nx.has_path(g, j, i):  # lowest_ix node from which i is reachable
185.                     if not nx.has_path(g, j, pi[i]):  # parent not reachable. Bad! (note nx considers each node as having a path to itself)
186.                         return False
187.                     else:
188.                         break  # this parent is ok! advance to outermost for loop
189.     return True

193. def is_acyclic(pi):
194.     """
195.     Function to check for cycles in a predecessor array returned by the model
196.     :param input: the adjacency matrix of the graph on which the model has inferred the predecessor array
197.     :param pi: the predecessor array

199.     """
200.     ts = gl.TopologicalSorter()
201.     for i in range(len(pi)):
202.         ts.add(i, pi[i])
203.     try:
204.         ts.prepare()
205.         return True
206.     except ValueError as e:
207.         if isinstance(e, gl.CycleError):
208.             #print("I am a cycle error")
209.             return False
210.         else:
211.             raise e

228. def bellman_ford_cost(A, s):
229.   """Bellman-Ford's single-source shortest path (Bellman, 1958).
230.   This has been taken and adapted from the original CLRS Bellman-Ford implementation"""
231. 
232. 
233.   chex.assert_rank(A, 2)
234. 
235.   A_pos = np.arange(A.shape[0])
236. 
237.   d = np.zeros(A.shape[0])
238.   pi = np.arange(A.shape[0])
239.   msk = np.zeros(A.shape[0])
240.   d[s] = 0
241.   msk[s] = 1
242.   while True:
243.     prev_d = np.copy(d)
244.     prev_msk = np.copy(msk)
245.     for u in range(A.shape[0]):
246.       for v in range(A.shape[0]):
247.         if prev_msk[u] == 1 and A[u, v] != 0:
248.           if msk[v] == 0 or prev_d[u] + A[u, v] < d[v]:
249.             d[v] = prev_d[u] + A[u, v]
250.             pi[v] = u
251.           msk[v] = 1
252.     if np.all(d == prev_d):
253.       break
254.   return d

256. def check_valid_BFpaths(A,s, parentpath):
257.     ''' 1. Computes true shortest path costs,
258.         2. Builds BF parent-tree subgraph of graph, computes shortest path costs on subgraph (model's paths)
259.     Note self-parent (pi[t] = t) is the default for no path s->t. '''
260. 
261.     true_costs = bellman_ford_cost(A,s)
262.     parentpath = np.array(parentpath).astype(int)
263. 
264.     # the adjacency matrix of the BF tree
265.     BF_tree_adj = np.zeros((len(parentpath),len(parentpath)))
266.     for i in range(len(parentpath)):
267.         #if parentpath[i] == i and i != s: # shortest path. forbids neg. weight cycle solutions
268.         #    return False
269.         #breakpoint()
270.         if A[parentpath[i],i] == 0 and parentpath[i] != i: # you're allowed to pick self-parents for unreachable nodes
271.             return False
272.         else:
273.             BF_tree_adj[parentpath[i],i] = A[parentpath[i],i]
274. 
275.     model_costs = bellman_ford_cost(BF_tree_adj, s)
276. 
277.     if (true_costs == model_costs).all():
278.         return True
279.     else:
280.         return False

306. def check_valid_bfsTree(A, pi, s):
307.     pi = copy.deepcopy(pi) # copy pi to avoid mutation
308. 
309.     # pi should have same length as number of nodes in A
310.     assert len(pi) == A.shape[0], "pi length must match number of nodes in A"
311. 
312.     # Compute shortest path distances from s in A
313.     G = nx.from_numpy_array(A, create_using=nx.Graph)
314.     dist = nx.single_source_shortest_path_length(G, s)
315. 
316.     # Source node must be its own parent
317.     if pi[s] != s:
318.         return False
319. 
320.     # Unreachable nodes must have self-parent
321.     # Reachable nodes have valid parents and correct levels
322.     for i in range(len(pi)):
323.         if i == s:
324.             continue  # already checked source node
325.         if i not in dist:  # unreachable
326.             if pi[i] != i:
327.                 return False
328.         else:  # reachable
329.             parent = pi[i]
330.             if parent == i:  # self-parent not allowed for reachable nodes
331.                 return False
332.             if A[parent][i] == 0:  # no edge from parent to child
333.                 return False
334.             if dist[parent] != dist[i] - 1:  # parent must be one level above child
335.                 return False
336.             
337.     return True
338.
```

```
217. def BF_greedysearch(A, s, probMatrix, beamwidth=3):
218.     pi = np.zeros(len(probMatrix))
219.     pi[s] = s
220. 
221.     # sample parents for each non-source node
222.     for i in range(len(probMatrix)):
223.         if i != s:
224.             # sample candidate parents, ensure at least one parent is plausible (there exists an edge (parent,i))
225.             candidates_costs = np.full(beamwidth, np.inf)
226.             counter = 0
227.             while (candidates_costs == np.full(len(candidates_costs), np.inf)).all() and counter < 10:
228.                 candidates = [dfs_sampling.chooseUniformly(probMatrix[i]) for j in range(beamwidth)]
229.                 candidates_costs =[A[candidate, i] for candidate in candidates]

231.                 for k in range(len(candidates_costs)):
232.                     if candidates_costs[k] == 0:
233.                         candidates_costs[k] = np.inf
234.                 counter += 1
235. 
236.             # choose lowest-cost parent
237.             pi[i] = candidates[np.argmin(candidates_costs)]
238.     return pi
```

def extract(pdf_path):
    text=''
    err=''
    try:

```
16. """Algorithm specs.
17. 
18. The "spec" of each algorithm is a static set of `(stage, loc, type)`-tuples.
19. 
20. - `stage`: One of either an `input`, `output` or `hint`
21. - `location`: Each datum is associated with either the `node`, `edge` or `graph`
22. - `type`: Either a `scalar`, `categorical`, `mask`, `mask_one` or `pointer`
23. 
24. The dataflow for an algorithm is represented by `(stage, loc, type, data)`
25. "probes" that are valid under that algorithm's spec. It contains a single
26. snapshot for each `input` and `output` and a time-series of intermediate
27. algorithmic states (`hint`).
28. 
29. At minimum, each node contains a `pos` probe that serves as a unique index e.g.
```

```
80.       algorithm: The algorithm to sample from
81.       spec: The algorithm spec.
82.       num_samples: Number of algorithm unrolls to sample. If positive, all the
83.         samples will be generated in the constructor, and at each call
84.         of the `next` method a batch will be randomly selected among them.
85.         If -1, samples are generated on the fly with each call to `next`.
86.       *args: Algorithm args.

88.       **kwargs: Algorithm kwargs.
89.     """
90. 
91.     # Use `RandomState` to ensure deterministic sampling across Numpy versions.
92.     self._rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
93.     self._spec = spec
94.     self._num_samples = num_samples
95.     self._algorithm = algorithm
96.     self._args = args
97.     self._kwargs = kwargs
98. 
99.     if num_samples < 0:
100.       logging.warning('Sampling dataset on-the-fly, unlimited samples.')
101.       # Just get an initial estimate of max hint length
102.       self.max_steps = -1
103.       for _ in range(1000):
104.         data = self._sample_data(*args, **kwargs)
105.         _, probes = algorithm(*data)
106.         _, _, hint = probing.split_stages(probes, spec)
107.         for dp in hint:
108.           assert dp.data.shape[1] == 1  # batching axis
109.           if dp.data.shape[0] > self.max_steps:
110.             self.max_steps = dp.data.shape[0]
111.     else:
112.       logging.info('Creating a dataset with %i samples.', num_samples)
113.       (self._inputs, self._outputs, self._hints,
114.        self._lengths) = self._make_batch(num_samples, spec, 0, algorithm, *args,
115.                                          **kwargs)

117.   def _make_batch(self, num_samples: int, spec: specs.Spec, min_length: int,
118.                   algorithm: Algorithm, *args, **kwargs):
119.     """Generate a batch of data."""
120.     inputs = []
121.     outputs = []
122.     hints = []
123. 
124.     for _ in range(num_samples):
125.       data = self._sample_data(*args, **kwargs)
126.       _, probes = algorithm(*data)
127.       inp, outp, hint = probing.split_stages(probes, spec)
128.       inputs.append(inp)
129.       outputs.append(outp)
130.       hints.append(hint)
131.       if len(hints) % 1000 == 0:
132.         logging.info('%i samples created', len(hints))
133. 
134.     # Batch and pad trajectories to max(T).
135.     inputs = _batch_io(inputs)
136.     outputs = _batch_io(outputs)
137.     hints, lengths = _batch_hints(hints, min_length)
138.     print(f"Inputs: {inputs}, Outputs: {outputs}, Hints: {hints}, Lengths: {lengths}, Algo: {algorithm}")
139.     return inputs, outputs, hints, lengths

141.   def next(self, batch_size: Optional[int] = None) -> Feedback:
142.     """Subsamples trajectories from the pre-generated dataset.
143. 
144.     Args:
145.       batch_size: Optional batch size. If `None`, returns entire dataset.
146. 
147.     Returns:
148.       Subsampled trajectories.
149.     """
150.     if batch_size:

152.         inputs, outputs, hints, lengths = self._make_batch(

154.             self._algorithm, *self._args, **self._kwargs)
155.         if hints[0].data.shape[0] > self.max_steps:
156.           logging.warning('Increasing hint lengh from %i to %i',
157.                           self.max_steps, hints[0].data.shape[0])
158.           self.max_steps = hints[0].data.shape[0]
159.       else:
160.         if batch_size > self._num_samples:
161.           raise ValueError(
162.               f'Batch size {batch_size} > dataset size {self._num_samples}.')
163. 
164.         # Returns a fixed-size random batch.
165.         indices = self._rng.choice(self._num_samples, (batch_size,),
166.                                    replace=True)
167.         inputs = _subsample_data(self._inputs, indices, axis=0)
168.         outputs = _subsample_data(self._outputs, indices, axis=0)
169.         hints = _subsample_data(self._hints, indices, axis=1)
170.         lengths = self._lengths[indices]
171. 
172.     else:
173.       # Returns the full dataset.
174.       assert self._num_samples >= 0
175.       inputs = self._inputs
176.       hints = self._hints
177.       lengths = self._lengths
178.       outputs = self._outputs
179. 
180.     return Feedback(Features(inputs, hints, lengths), outputs)
```

35. def log_sinkhorn(x: _Array, steps: int, temperature: float, zero_diagonal: bool,
36.                  noise_rng_key: Optional[_Array]) -> _Array:
37.   """Sinkhorn operator in log space, to postprocess permutation pointer logits.
38. 
39.   Args:
40.     x: input of shape [..., n, n], a batch of square matrices.
41.     steps: number of iterations.
42.     temperature: temperature parameter (as temperature approaches zero, the
43.       output approaches a permutation matrix).
44.     zero_diagonal: whether to force the diagonal logits towards -inf.
45.     noise_rng_key: key to add Gumbel noise.
46. 
47.   Returns:
48.     Elementwise logarithm of a doubly-stochastic matrix (a matrix with
49.     non-negative elements whose rows and columns sum to 1).
50.   """
51.   assert x.ndim >= 2
52.   assert x.shape[-1] == x.shape[-2]
53.   if noise_rng_key is not None:
54.     # Add standard Gumbel noise (see https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.08665)
55.     noise = -jnp.log(-jnp.log(jax.random.uniform(noise_rng_key,
56.                                                  x.shape) + 1e-12) + 1e-12)
57.     x = x + noise
58.   x /= temperature
59.   if zero_diagonal:
60.     x = x - 1e6 * jnp.eye(x.shape[-1])
61.   for _ in range(steps):
62.     x = jax.nn.log_softmax(x, axis=-1)
63.     x = jax.nn.log_softmax(x, axis=-2)
64.   return x
65.

129. def postprocess(spec: _Spec, preds: Dict[str, _Array],
130.                 sinkhorn_temperature: float,
131.                 sinkhorn_steps: int,
132.                 hard: bool) -> Dict[str, _DataPoint]:
133.   """Postprocesses decoder output.
134. 
135.   This is done on outputs in order to score performance, and on hints in
136.   order to score them but also in order to feed them back to the model.
137.   At scoring time, the postprocessing mode is "hard", logits will be
138.   arg-maxed and masks will be thresholded. However, for the case of the hints
139.   that are fed back in the model, the postprocessing can be hard or soft,
140.   depending on whether we want to let gradients flow through them or not.
141. 
142.   Args:
143.     spec: The spec of the algorithm whose outputs/hints we are postprocessing.
144.     preds: Output and/or hint predictions, as produced by decoders.
145.     sinkhorn_temperature: Parameter for the sinkhorn operator on permutation
146.       pointers.
147.     sinkhorn_steps: Parameter for the sinkhorn operator on permutation
148.       pointers.
149.     hard: whether to do hard postprocessing, which involves argmax for
150.       MASK_ONE, CATEGORICAL and POINTERS, thresholding for MASK, and stop
151.       gradient through for SCALAR. If False, soft postprocessing will be used,
152.       with softmax, sigmoid and gradients allowed.
153.   Returns:
154.     The postprocessed `preds`. In "soft" post-processing, POINTER types will
155.     change to SOFT_POINTER, so encoders know they do not need to be
156.     pre-processed before feeding them back in.
157.   """
158.   result = {}
159.   for name in preds.keys():
160.     _, loc, t = spec[name]
161.     new_t = t
162.     data = preds[name]
163.     if t == _Type.SCALAR:
164.       if hard:
165.         data = jax.lax.stop_gradient(data)
166.     elif t == _Type.MASK:
167.       if hard:
168.         data = (data > 0.0) * 1.0
169.       else:
170.         data = jax.nn.sigmoid(data)
171.     elif t in [_Type.MASK_ONE, _Type.CATEGORICAL]:
172.       cat_size = data.shape[-1]
173.       if hard:
174.         best = jnp.argmax(data, -1)
175.         data = hk.one_hot(best, cat_size)
176.       else:
177.         data = jax.nn.softmax(data, axis=-1)
178.     elif t == _Type.POINTER:
179.       if hard:
180.         #print('decoders.py, postprocess: ', data)
181.         data = jnp.argmax(data, -1).astype(float)
182.       else:
183.         data = jax.nn.softmax(data, -1)
184.         new_t = _Type.SOFT_POINTER
185.     elif t == _Type.PERMUTATION_POINTER:
186.       # Convert the matrix of logits to a doubly stochastic matrix.
187.       data = log_sinkhorn(
188.           x=data,
189.           steps=sinkhorn_steps,
190.           temperature=sinkhorn_temperature,
191.           zero_diagonal=True,
192.           noise_rng_key=None)
193.       data = jnp.exp(data)
194.       if hard:
195.         data = jax.nn.one_hot(jnp.argmax(data, axis=-1), data.shape[-1])
196.     elif t == _Type.MULT_SOL:
197.       #pass
198.       data = jax.nn.softmax(data) # verify shape=[batch,nodes,nodes]
199.       # values should be logits?
200.     else:
201.       raise ValueError("Invalid type")
202.     result[name] = probing.DataPoint(
203.         name=name, location=loc, type_=new_t, data=data)
204. 
205.   return result
206.

208. def decode_fts(
209.     decoders,
210.     spec: _Spec,
211.     h_t: _Array,
212.     adj_mat: _Array,
213.     edge_fts: _Array,
214.     graph_fts: _Array,
215.     inf_bias: bool,
216.     inf_bias_edge: bool,
217.     repred: bool,
218. ):
219.   """Decodes node, edge and graph features."""
220.   output_preds = {}
221.   hint_preds = {}
222. 
223.   for name in decoders:
224.     decoder = decoders[name]
225.     stage, loc, t = spec[name]
226. 
227.     if loc == _Location.NODE:
228.       preds = _decode_node_fts(decoder, t, h_t, edge_fts, adj_mat,
229.                                inf_bias, repred)
230.     elif loc == _Location.EDGE:
231.       preds = _decode_edge_fts(decoder, t, h_t, edge_fts, adj_mat,
232.                                inf_bias_edge)
233.     elif loc == _Location.GRAPH:
234.       preds = _decode_graph_fts(decoder, t, h_t, graph_fts)
235.     else:
236.       raise ValueError("Invalid output type")
237. 
238.     if stage == _Stage.OUTPUT:
239.       output_preds[name] = preds
240.     elif stage == _Stage.HINT:
241.       hint_preds[name] = preds
242.     else:
243.       raise ValueError(f"Found unexpected decoder {name}")
244. 
245.   return hint_preds, output_preds
246.

248. def _decode_node_fts(decoders, t: str, h_t: _Array, edge_fts: _Array,
249.                      adj_mat: _Array, inf_bias: bool, repred: bool) -> _Array:
250.   """Decodes node features."""
251. 
252.   if t in [_Type.SCALAR, _Type.MASK, _Type.MASK_ONE]:
253.     preds = jnp.squeeze(decoders[0](h_t), -1)
254.   elif t == _Type.CATEGORICAL:
255.     preds = decoders[0](h_t)
256.   elif t == _Type.MULT_SOL:
257.     # breakpoint() weird! if you have this breakpoint and continue, you get an error. But run without, no error arises
258.     p_1 = decoders[0](h_t)  # from vector:  shape [batch,nodes,hidden]
259.     p_2 = decoders[1](h_t)  # to vector:  shape [batch,nodes,hidden]
260.     p_3 = decoders[2](edge_fts)  # edge features: [batch,nodes,nodes,hidden]

32. def construct_encoders(stage: str, loc: str, t: str,
33.                        hidden_dim: int, init: str, name: str):
34.   """Constructs encoders."""
35.   if init == 'xavier_on_scalars' and stage == _Stage.HINT and t == _Type.SCALAR:
36.     initialiser = hk.initializers.TruncatedNormal(
37.         stddev=1.0 / jnp.sqrt(hidden_dim))
38.   elif init in ['default', 'xavier_on_scalars']:
39.     initialiser = None
40.   else:
41.     raise ValueError(f'Encoder initialiser {init} not supported.')
42.   linear = functools.partial(
43.       hk.Linear,
44.       w_init=initialiser,
45.       name=f'{name}_enc_linear')
46.   encoders = [linear(hidden_dim)]
47.   if loc == _Location.EDGE and t == _Type.POINTER:
48.     # Edge pointers need two-way encoders.
49.     encoders.append(linear(hidden_dim))
50. 
51.   return encoders
52. 
53. 
54. def preprocess(dp: _DataPoint, nb_nodes: int) -> _DataPoint:
55.   """Pre-process data point.
56. 
57.   Make sure that the data is ready to be encoded into features.
58.   If the data is of POINTER type, we expand the compressed index representation
59.   to a full one-hot. But if the data is a SOFT_POINTER, the representation
60.   is already expanded and we just overwrite the type as POINTER so that
61.   it is treated as such for encoding.
62. 
63.   Args:
64.     dp: A DataPoint to prepare for encoding.
65.     nb_nodes: Number of nodes in the graph, necessary to expand pointers to
66.       the right dimension.
67.   Returns:
68.     The datapoint, with data and possibly type modified.
69.   """
70.   new_type = dp.type_
71.   if dp.type_ == _Type.POINTER:
72.     data = hk.one_hot(dp.data, nb_nodes)
73.   else:
74.     data = dp.data.astype(jnp.float32)
75.     if dp.type_ == _Type.SOFT_POINTER:
76.       new_type = _Type.POINTER
77.   dp = probing.DataPoint(
78.       name=dp.name, location=dp.location, type_=new_type, data=data)
79. 
80.   return dp
81. 
82. 
83. def accum_adj_mat(dp: _DataPoint, adj_mat: _Array) -> _Array:
84.   """Accumulates adjacency matrix."""
85.   if dp.location == _Location.NODE and dp.type_ in [_Type.POINTER,
86.                                                     _Type.PERMUTATION_POINTER]:
87.     adj_mat += ((dp.data + jnp.transpose(dp.data, (0, 2, 1))) > 0.5)
88.   elif dp.location == _Location.EDGE and dp.type_ == _Type.MASK:
89.     adj_mat += ((dp.data + jnp.transpose(dp.data, (0, 2, 1))) > 0.0)
90. 
91.   return (adj_mat > 0.).astype('float32')  # pytype: disable=attribute-error  # numpy-scalars
92. 
93. 
94. def accum_edge_fts(encoders, dp: _DataPoint, edge_fts: _Array) -> _Array:
95.   """Encodes and accumulates edge features."""
96.   if dp.location == _Location.NODE and dp.type_ in [_Type.POINTER,
97.                                                     _Type.PERMUTATION_POINTER]:
98.     encoding = _encode_inputs(encoders, dp)
99.     edge_fts += encoding
100. 
101.   elif dp.location == _Location.EDGE:
102.     encoding = _encode_inputs(encoders, dp)
103.     if dp.type_ == _Type.POINTER:
104.       # Aggregate pointer contributions across sender and receiver nodes.
105.       encoding_2 = encoders[1](jnp.expand_dims(dp.data, -1))
106.       edge_fts += jnp.mean(encoding, axis=1) + jnp.mean(encoding_2, axis=2)
107.     else:
108.       edge_fts += encoding
109. 
110.   return edge_fts
111. 
112. 
113. def accum_node_fts(encoders, dp: _DataPoint, node_fts: _Array) -> _Array:
114.   """Encodes and accumulates node features."""
115.   is_pointer = (dp.type_ in [_Type.POINTER, _Type.PERMUTATION_POINTER])
116.   if ((dp.location == _Location.NODE and not is_pointer) or
117.       (dp.location == _Location.GRAPH and dp.type_ == _Type.POINTER)):
118.     encoding = _encode_inputs(encoders, dp)
119.     node_fts += encoding
120. 
121.   return node_fts
122. 
123. 
124. def accum_graph_fts(encoders, dp: _DataPoint,
125.                     graph_fts: _Array) -> _Array:
126.   """Encodes and accumulates graph features."""
127.   if dp.location == _Location.GRAPH and dp.type_ != _Type.POINTER:
128.     encoding = _encode_inputs(encoders, dp)
129.     graph_fts += encoding
130. 
131.   return graph_fts
132. 
133. 
134. def _encode_inputs(encoders, dp: _DataPoint) -> _Array:
135.   if dp.type_ == _Type.CATEGORICAL:
136.     encoding = encoders[0](dp.data)
137.   else:
138.     encoding = encoders[0](jnp.expand_dims(dp.data, -1))
139.   return encoding
140.

77. def _pmap_reshape(x, n_devices, split_axis=0):
78.   """Splits a pytree over n_devices on axis split_axis for pmapping."""
79.   def _reshape(arr):
80.     new_shape = (arr.shape[:split_axis] +
81.                  (n_devices, arr.shape[split_axis] // n_devices) +
82.                  arr.shape[split_axis + 1:])
83.     return jnp.moveaxis(jnp.reshape(arr, new_shape), split_axis, 0)
84.   return jax.tree_util.tree_map(_reshape, x)

94. @functools.partial(jax.jit, static_argnums=1)
95. def _pmap_data(data: Union[_Feedback, _Features], n_devices: int):
96.   """Replicate/split feedback or features for pmapping."""
97.   if isinstance(data, _Feedback):
98.     features = data.features
99.   else:
100.     features = data
101.   pmap_data = features._replace(
102.       inputs=_pmap_reshape(features.inputs, n_devices),
103.       hints=_pmap_reshape(features.hints, n_devices, split_axis=1),
104.       lengths=_pmap_reshape(features.lengths, n_devices),
105.   )
106.   if isinstance(data, _Feedback):
107.     pmap_data = data._replace(
108.         features=pmap_data,
109.         outputs=_pmap_reshape(data.outputs, n_devices)
110.     )
111.   return pmap_data

128. def _maybe_pmap_rng_key(rng_key: _Array):

133.   return jax.device_put_sharded(list(pmap_rng_keys), jax.local_devices())
