151.     model_sample_greedy = sample_greedysearch(As, source_nodes, [preds])
152.     true_sample_greedy = sample_greedysearch(As, source_nodes, outputs)
153. 
154.     model_greedy_truthmask = [check_graphs.check_valid_BFpaths(As[i], source_nodes[i], model_sample_greedy[i]) for i in
155.                             range(len(model_sample_greedy))]
156.     correctness_model_greedy = sum(model_greedy_truthmask) / len(model_greedy_truthmask)
157. 
158.     true_greedy_truthmask = [check_graphs.check_valid_BFpaths(As[i], source_nodes[i], true_sample_greedy[i]) for i in
159.                            range(len(model_sample_random))]
160.     correctness_true_greedy = sum(true_greedy_truthmask) / len(true_greedy_truthmask)
161. 
162.     model_greedy_uniques, model_greedy_valids_uniques, model_greedy_valids = check_uniqueness_bf(As = As, source_nodes = source_nodes,
163.         probMatrices=[preds], method = "greedy")
164.     true_greedy_uniques, true_greedy_valids_uniques, true_greedy_valids = check_uniqueness_bf(As = As, source_nodes = source_nodes,
165.         probMatrices=outputs, method = "greedy")
166. 
167. 
168.     ### LOGGING ###
169.     As = [i.flatten() for i in As]
170.     result_dict = {"As": As,
171.                    #
172.                    "Argmax_Model_Trees": model_sample_argmax,
173.                    "Argmax_True_Trees": true_sample_argmax,
174.                    #
175.                    "Argmax_Model_Mask": model_argmax_truthmask,
176.                    "Argmax_True_Mask": true_argmax_truthmask,
177.                    #
178.                    "Argmax_Model_Accuracy": correctness_model_argmax,
179.                    "Argmax_True_Accuracy": correctness_true_argmax,
180.                    #
181.                    ###
182.                    #
183.                    "Random_Model_Trees": model_sample_random,
184.                    "Random_True_Trees": true_sample_random,
185.                    #
186.                    "Random_Model_Mask": model_random_truthmask,
187.                    "Random_True_Mask": true_random_truthmask,
188.                    #
189.                    "Random_Model_Accuracy": correctness_model_random,
190.                    "Random_True_Accuracy": correctness_true_random,
191.                    #
192.                    ###
193.                    #
194.                    "Beam_Model_Trees": model_sample_beam,
195.                    "Beam_True_Trees": true_sample_beam,
196.                    #
197.                    "Beam_Model_Mask": model_beam_truthmask,
198.                    "Beam_True_Mask": true_beam_truthmask,
199.                    #
200.                    "Beam_Model_Accuracy": correctness_model_beam,
201.                    "Beam_True_Accuracy": correctness_true_beam,
202. 
203.                    "Beam_Model_Uniques": model_beam_uniques,
204.                    "Beam_Model_Valids_Uniques": model_beam_valids_uniques,
205.                    "Beam_Model_Valids": model_beam_valids,
206. 
207.                    "Beam_True_Uniques": true_beam_uniques,
208.                    "Beam_True_Valids_Uniques": true_beam_valids_uniques,
209.                    "Beam_True_Valids": true_beam_valids,
210.                    #
211.                    ###
212.                    #
213.                    "Greedy_Model_Trees": model_sample_greedy,
214.                    "Greedy_True_Trees": true_sample_greedy,
215.                    #
216.                    "Greedy_Model_Mask": model_greedy_truthmask,
217.                    "Greedy_True_Mask": true_greedy_truthmask,
218.                    #
219.                    "Greedy_Model_Accuracy": correctness_model_greedy,
220.                    "Greedy_True_Accuracy": correctness_true_greedy,
221. 
222.                    "Greedy_Model_Uniques":model_greedy_uniques,
223.                    "Greedy_Model_Valids_Uniques": model_greedy_valids_uniques,
224.                    "Greedy_Model_Valids": model_greedy_valids,
225. 
226.                    "Greedy_True_Uniques": true_greedy_uniques,
227.                    "Greedy_True_Valids_Uniques": true_greedy_valids_uniques,
228.                    "Greedy_True_Valids": true_greedy_valids
229.                    #
230.                    }
231.     save_results(result_dict, f"{filename}_BF")
232. 
233.     if extras:
234.         out.update(extras)
235.     return {k: unpack(v) for k, v in out.items()}
236. 
237. 
238. ###############################################################
239. # BFS Multi-Solution
240. ###############################################################
241. 
242. def BFS_multi_collect_and_eval(sampler, predict_fn, sample_count, rng_key, extras, 
243.                                 filename='bfs_accuracy', vd_flag=False, NSE=100):
244.     """Collect batches of output and hint preds and evaluate BFS multi-solution."""
245.     processed_samples = 0
246.     preds = []
247.     outputs = []
248.     As = []
249.     source_nodes = []
250.     
251.     while processed_samples < sample_count:
252.         feedback = next(sampler)
253.         batch_size = feedback.outputs[0].data.shape[0]
254.         outputs.append(feedback.outputs)
255.         new_rng_key, rng_key = jax.random.split(rng_key)
256.         cur_preds, _ = predict_fn(new_rng_key, feedback.features)
257.         preds.append(cur_preds)
258.         processed_samples += batch_size
259.         
260.         # BFS: feedback[0][0][1] is 's' (source), feedback[0][0][2] is 'A' (adjacency)
261.         As.append(feedback[0][0][2].data)
262.         source_nodes.append(np.argmax(feedback[0][0][1].data, axis=1))
263.     
264.     outputs = _concat(outputs, axis=0)
265.     As = _concat(As, axis=0)
266.     source_nodes = _concat(source_nodes, axis=0)
267.     preds = _concat(preds, axis=0)
268.     
269.     # Standard CLRS evaluation
270.     out = clrs.evaluate(outputs, preds)
271. 
272.     # === CATEGORICAL SAMPLING ===
273.     model_sample_categorical = bfs_sampling.sample_bfs_categorical([preds])
274.     true_sample_categorical = bfs_sampling.sample_bfs_categorical(outputs)
275. 
276.     model_categorical_truthmask = [
277.         check_graphs.check_valid_bfsTree(As[i], model_sample_categorical[i], s=source_nodes[i]) 
278.         for i in range(len(model_sample_categorical))
279.     ]
280.     correctness_model_categorical = sum(model_categorical_truthmask) / len(model_categorical_truthmask) 
281. 
282.     true_categorical_truthmask = [
283.         check_graphs.check_valid_bfsTree(As[i], true_sample_categorical[i], s=source_nodes[i]) 
284.         for i in range(len(true_sample_categorical))
285.     ]   
286.     correctness_true_categorical = sum(true_categorical_truthmask) / len(true_categorical_truthmask)
287.     
288.     # === RANDOM SAMPLING ===
289.     model_sample_random = dfs_sampling.sample_random_list([preds])
290.     true_sample_random = dfs_sampling.sample_random_list(outputs)
291.     
292.     model_random_truthmask = [
293.         check_graphs.check_valid_bfsTree(As[i], model_sample_random[i], s=source_nodes[i]) 
294.         for i in range(len(model_sample_random))
295.     ]
296.     correctness_model_random = sum(model_random_truthmask) / len(model_random_truthmask)
297.     
298.     true_random_truthmask = [
299.         check_graphs.check_valid_bfsTree(As[i], true_sample_random[i], s=source_nodes[i]) 
300.         for i in range(len(true_sample_random))
301.     ]
302.     correctness_true_random = sum(true_random_truthmask) / len(true_random_truthmask)
303.     
304.     # === PRIM-LIKE SAMPLING (BFS-specific) ===
305.     model_sample_prim = bfs_sampling.sample_bfs_prim([preds], source_nodes)
306.     true_sample_prim = bfs_sampling.sample_bfs_prim(outputs, source_nodes)
307.     
308.     model_prim_truthmask = [
309.         check_graphs.check_valid_bfsTree(As[i], model_sample_prim[i], s=source_nodes[i])
310.         for i in range(len(model_sample_prim))
311.     ]
312.     correctness_model_prim = sum(model_prim_truthmask) / len(model_prim_truthmask)
313.     
314.     true_prim_truthmask = [
315.         check_graphs.check_valid_bfsTree(As[i], true_sample_prim[i], s=source_nodes[i])
316.         for i in range(len(true_sample_prim))
317.     ]
318.     correctness_true_prim = sum(true_prim_truthmask) / len(true_prim_truthmask)
319.     
320.     # === BEAM SEARCH SAMPLING (BFS-specific) ===
```

</details>

242. def BFS_multi_collect_and_eval(sampler, predict_fn, sample_count, rng_key, extras, 
243.                                 filename='bfs_accuracy', vd_flag=False, NSE=100):
244.     """Collect batches of output and hint preds and evaluate BFS multi-solution."""
245.     processed_samples = 0
246.     preds = []
247.     outputs = []
248.     As = []
249.     source_nodes = []
250.     
251.     while processed_samples < sample_count:
252.         feedback = next(sampler)
253.         batch_size = feedback.outputs[0].data.shape[0]
254.         outputs.append(feedback.outputs)
255.         new_rng_key, rng_key = jax.random.split(rng_key)
256.         cur_preds, _ = predict_fn(new_rng_key, feedback.features)
257.         preds.append(cur_preds)
258.         processed_samples += batch_size
259.         
260.         # BFS: feedback[0][0][1] is 's' (source), feedback[0][0][2] is 'A' (adjacency)
261.         As.append(feedback[0][0][2].data)
262.         source_nodes.append(np.argmax(feedback[0][0][1].data, axis=1))
263.     
264.     outputs = _concat(outputs, axis=0)
265.     As = _concat(As, axis=0)
266.     source_nodes = _concat(source_nodes, axis=0)
267.     preds = _concat(preds, axis=0)
268.     
269.     # Standard CLRS evaluation
270.     out = clrs.evaluate(outputs, preds)
271. 
272.     # === CATEGORICAL SAMPLING ===
273.     model_sample_categorical = bfs_sampling.sample_bfs_categorical([preds])
274.     true_sample_categorical = bfs_sampling.sample_bfs_categorical(outputs)
275. 
276.     model_categorical_truthmask = [
277.         check_graphs.check_valid_bfsTree(As[i], model_sample_categorical[i], s=source_nodes[i]) 
278.         for i in range(len(model_sample_categorical))
279.     ]
280.     correctness_model_categorical = sum(model_categorical_truthmask) / len(model_categorical_truthmask) 
281. 
282.     true_categorical_truthmask = [
283.         check_graphs.check_valid_bfsTree(As[i], true_sample_categorical[i], s=source_nodes[i]) 
284.         for i in range(len(true_sample_categorical))
285.     ]   
286.     correctness_true_categorical = sum(true_categorical_truthmask) / len(true_categorical_truthmask)
287.     
288.     # === RANDOM SAMPLING ===
289.     model_sample_random = dfs_sampling.sample_random_list([preds])
290.     true_sample_random = dfs_sampling.sample_random_list(outputs)
291.     
292.     model_random_truthmask = [
293.         check_graphs.check_valid_bfsTree(As[i], model_sample_random[i], s=source_nodes[i]) 
294.         for i in range(len(model_sample_random))
295.     ]
296.     correctness_model_random = sum(model_random_truthmask) / len(model_random_truthmask)
297.     
298.     true_random_truthmask = [
299.         check_graphs.check_valid_bfsTree(As[i], true_sample_random[i], s=source_nodes[i]) 
300.         for i in range(len(true_sample_random))
301.     ]
302.     correctness_true_random = sum(true_random_truthmask) / len(true_random_truthmask)
303.     
304.     # === PRIM-LIKE SAMPLING (BFS-specific) ===
305.     model_sample_prim = bfs_sampling.sample_bfs_prim([preds], source_nodes)
306.     true_sample_prim = bfs_sampling.sample_bfs_prim(outputs, source_nodes)
307.     
308.     model_prim_truthmask = [
309.         check_graphs.check_valid_bfsTree(As[i], model_sample_prim[i], s=source_nodes[i])
310.         for i in range(len(model_sample_prim))
311.     ]
312.     correctness_model_prim = sum(model_prim_truthmask) / len(model_prim_truthmask)
313.     
314.     true_prim_truthmask = [
315.         check_graphs.check_valid_bfsTree(As[i], true_sample_prim[i], s=source_nodes[i])
316.         for i in range(len(true_sample_prim))
317.     ]
318.     correctness_true_prim = sum(true_prim_truthmask) / len(true_prim_truthmask)
319.     
320.     # === BEAM SEARCH SAMPLING (BFS-specific) ===
321.     model_sample_beam = bfs_sampling.sample_bfs_beam([preds], source_nodes, beam_width=3)
322.     true_sample_beam = bfs_sampling.sample_bfs_beam(outputs, source_nodes, beam_width=3)
323.     
324.     model_beam_truthmask = [
325.         check_graphs.check_valid_bfsTree(As[i], model_sample_beam[i], s=source_nodes[i])
326.         for i in range(len(model_sample_beam))
327.     ]
328.     correctness_model_beam = sum(model_beam_truthmask) / len(model_beam_truthmask)
329.

332.         for i in range(len(true_sample_beam))
333.     ]
334.     correctness_true_beam = sum(true_beam_truthmask) / len(true_beam_truthmask)
335.

342.         #

344.         "Categorical_True_Trees": true_sample_categorical,

353.         "Random_True_Mask": true_random_truthmask,
354.         "Random_Model_Accuracy": correctness_model_random,
355.         "Random_True_Accuracy": correctness_true_random,
356.         #

358.         "Prim_True_Trees": true_sample_prim,
359.         "Prim_Model_Mask": model_prim_truthmask,
360.         "Prim_True_Mask": true_prim_truthmask,
361.         "Prim_Model_Accuracy": correctness_model_prim,
362.         "Prim_True_Accuracy": correctness_true_prim,
363.         #

367.         "Beam_True_Mask": true_beam_truthmask,
368.         "Beam_Model_Accuracy": correctness_model_beam,
369.         "Beam_True_Accuracy": correctness_true_beam,
370.     }
371.     save_results(result_dict, f"{filename}_BFS")
372.     
373.     if extras:
374.         out.update(extras)
375.     return {k: unpack(v) for k, v in out.items()}

1. import numpy as np
2. from clrs._src import dfs_sampling

4. def sample_bfs_prim(outsOrPreds, s_indices):
5.     """
6.     Samples BFS trees using a Prim-like greedy approach.
7.     
8.     Args:
9.         outsOrPreds: Model outputs containing parent probabilities.
10.         s_indices: List of source node indices for each graph in the batch.
11.         
12.     Returns:
13.         List of parent arrays (pi), one for each graph in the batch.
14.     """
15.     probMatrix_list = dfs_sampling.extract_probMatrices(outsOrPreds)
16.     pi_trees = []
17.     
18.     # Handle case where s_indices might be a single int or list
19.     if isinstance(s_indices, int):
20.         s_indices = [s_indices] * len(probMatrix_list)
21.         
22.     for i, probMatrix in enumerate(probMatrix_list):
23.         s = s_indices[i]
24.         pi = prim_like_sampler(probMatrix, s)
25.         pi_trees.append(pi)
26.         
27.     return pi_trees
28. 
29. def prim_like_sampler(probMatrix, s):
30.     """
31.     Constructs a BFS tree starting from the root, adding nodes that are most likely 
32.     connected to the current tree.
33.     
34.     Args:
35.         probMatrix: N x N matrix where P[i, j] is prob that j is parent of i.
36.         s: Source node index.
37.         
38.     Returns:
39.         pi: Array of length N, where pi[i] is the parent of i.
40.     """
41.     num_nodes = probMatrix.shape[0]
42.     pi = np.full(num_nodes, -1, dtype=int) # -1 indicates not yet processed/no parent
43.     pi[s] = s
44.     
45.     processed = {s}
46.     remaining = set(range(num_nodes)) - {s}
47.     
48.     # To optimize, we could maintain scores, but N is likely small (<= 64 usually in CLRS)
49.     # So recomputing sum might be fast enough.
50.     
51.     while remaining:
52.         best_v = -1
53.         best_score = -1.0
54.         
55.         # Find v in remaining with highest prob of attaching to processed set
56.         # score(v) = sum_{u in processed} P(parent(v) = u)
57.         for v in remaining:
58.             # probMatrix[v, u] is prob that u is parent of v.
59.             # We sum over u in processed.
60.             score = sum(probMatrix[v, u] for u in processed)
61.             
62.             if score > best_score:
63.                 best_score = score
64.                 best_v = v
65.         
66.         if best_v == -1:
67.             # This happens if remaining nodes have 0 prob of connecting to processed nodes
68.             # (disconnected graph components). 
69.             # We just pick one arbitrarily or handle it?
70.             # For BFS, disconnected nodes typically point to themselves or have 0 parent in some representations.
71.             # Here, let's just pick the first one and attach it to itself (or closest processed if any non-zero).
72.             best_v = list(remaining)[0]
73.             # If score is 0, it means no connection.
74.             # We'll just process it to avoid infinite loop.
75.             
76.         # Sample parent for best_v from processed set
77.         # Probabilities are P(parent(best_v) = u) for u in processed
78.         # We need to normalize these to sum to 1.
79.         
80.         candidate_parents = list(processed)
81.         probs = np.array([probMatrix[best_v, u] for u in candidate_parents])
82.         
83.         total_prob = probs.sum()
84.         if total_prob > 0:
85.             probs = probs / total_prob
86.             parent = np.random.choice(candidate_parents, p=probs)
87.         else:
88.             # No valid parent in processed set (disconnected). 
89.             # Default to self-loop or some fallback.
90.             parent = best_v 
91.             
92.         pi[best_v] = parent
93.         processed.add(best_v)
94.         remaining.remove(best_v)
95.         
96.     return pi
97. 
98. def sample_bfs_categorical(outsOrPreds):
99.     """
100.     Samples parent pointers independently for each node using categorical sampling.
101.     Note: This does NOT guarantee a tree structure (may contain cycles or orphans).
102.     
103.     Args:           
104.         outsOrPreds: Model outputs containing parent probabilities.
105.         
106.     Returns:
107.         List of parent arrays (pi).
108.     """
109.     probMatrix_list = dfs_sampling.extract_probMatrices(outsOrPreds)
110.     pi_trees = []
111.     
112.     for probMatrix in probMatrix_list:
113.         num_nodes = probMatrix.shape[0]
114.         pi = np.zeros(num_nodes, dtype=int)
115.         
116.         for i in range(num_nodes):
117.             # Sample parent for node i based on the distribution in row i
118.             probs = probMatrix[i]
119.             # Ensure probabilities sum to 1 for np.random.choice
120.             total_p = np.sum(probs)
121.             assert total_p >= 0, "Probabilities must be non-negative"
122.             if total_p > 0:
123.                 normalized_probs = probs / total_p
124.                 pi[i] = np.random.choice(num_nodes, p=normalized_probs)
125.                 
126.         pi_trees.append(pi)
127.         
128.     return pi_trees
129. 
130. def sample_bfs_beam(outsOrPreds, s_indices, beam_width=3):
131.     """
132.     Samples BFS trees using a Beam Search approach.
133.     
134.     Args:
135.         outsOrPreds: Model outputs containing parent probabilities.
136.         s_indices: List of source node indices.
137.         beam_width: Number of hypotheses to keep.
138.         
139.     Returns:
140.         List of parent arrays (pi).
141.     """
142.     probMatrix_list = dfs_sampling.extract_probMatrices(outsOrPreds)
143.     pi_trees = []
144.     
145.     if isinstance(s_indices, int):
146.         s_indices = [s_indices] * len(probMatrix_list)
147.         
148.     for i, probMatrix in enumerate(probMatrix_list):
149.         s = s_indices[i]
150.         pi = bfs_beam_sampler(probMatrix, s, beam_width)
151.         pi_trees.append(pi)
152.         
153.     return pi_trees
154. 
155. def bfs_beam_sampler(probMatrix, s, beam_width):
156.     num_nodes = probMatrix.shape[0]
157.     
158.     # State: (log_prob, pi_array, processed_set_as_tuple)
159.     # processed_set is stored as tuple for hashing/copying if needed, though sets are fine if we copy.
160.     # pi_array initialized with -1
161.     initial_pi = np.full(num_nodes, -1, dtype=int)
162.     initial_pi[s] = s
163.     
164.     # Beam: list of dicts or objects. 
165.     # Let's use a simple dict: {'log_prob': 0.0, 'pi': pi, 'processed': {s}}
166.     beam = [{'log_prob': 0.0, 'pi': initial_pi, 'processed': {s}}]
167.     
168.     # We need to add N-1 nodes
169.     for _ in range(num_nodes - 1):
170.         candidates = []
171.         
172.         for hyp in beam:
173.             processed = hyp['processed']
174.             pi = hyp['pi']
175.             curr_log_prob = hyp['log_prob']
176.             remaining = set(range(num_nodes)) - processed
177.             
178.             if not remaining:
179.                 candidates.append(hyp)
180.                 continue
181.             
182.             # 1. Select next node `v` to add (Greedy heuristic)
183.             # We pick the v with highest total probability of connecting to current processed set
184.             best_v = -1
185.             best_connection_mass = -1.0
186.             
187.             for v in remaining:
188.                 # Sum of probs from processed nodes to v
189.                 # probMatrix[v, u] is P(parent(v)=u)
190.                 mass = sum(probMatrix[v, u] for u in processed)
191.                 if mass > best_connection_mass:
192.                     best_connection_mass = mass
193.                     best_v = v
194.             
195.             if best_v == -1:
196.                 best_v = list(remaining)[0] # Disconnected/fallback
197.                 
198.             # 2. Branch on all possible parents u in processed for best_v
199.             possible_parents = list(processed)
200.             
201.             for u in possible_parents:
202.                 p_val = probMatrix[best_v, u]
203.                 if p_val > 1e-9: # Avoid log(0)
204.                     new_log_prob = curr_log_prob + np.log(p_val)
205.                 else:
206.                     new_log_prob = curr_log_prob - 1e9 # Penalty
207.                 
208.                 new_pi = pi.copy()
209.                 new_pi[best_v] = u
210.                 new_processed = processed.copy()
211.                 new_processed.add(best_v)
212.                 
213.                 candidates.append({
214.                     'log_prob': new_log_prob,
215.                     'pi': new_pi,
216.                     'processed': new_processed
217.                 })
218.         
219.         if not candidates:
220.             break # Should not happen usually unless disconnected
221. 
222.         # Select top-k candidates
223.         # Sort by log_prob descending
224.         candidates.sort(key=lambda x: x['log_prob'], reverse=True)
225.         beam = candidates[:beam_width]
226.         
227.     return beam[0]['pi'] # Return best hypothesis

1. """BFS plugin wiring for modular multi-solution evaluation."""
2. 
3. import copy
4. from typing import Dict
5. 
6. import clrs
7. import jax
8. import numpy as np
9. 
10. from clrs._src import dfs_sampling
11. from clrs._src.multi_sol.data.adapters import concat_tree
12. from clrs._src.multi_sol.evaluation import reports
13. from clrs._src.multi_sol.evaluation.runners import evaluate_sampling_pair
14. from clrs._src.multi_sol.sampling import bfs as bfs_sampling
15. from clrs._src.multi_sol.validation import bfs as bfs_validation
16. 
17. 
18. def evaluate_bfs_multisol_batch(
19.     sampler,
20.     predict_fn,
21.     sample_count,
22.     rng_key,
23.     extras,
24.     save_results_fn,
25.     filename="bfs_accuracy",
26. ) -> Dict[str, float]:
27.   """Collect, evaluate, sample, validate and save BFS multi-solution results."""
28.   processed_samples = 0
29.   preds = []
30.   outputs = []
31.   adjacency_batches = []
32.   source_batches = []
33. 
34.   while processed_samples < sample_count:
35.     feedback = next(sampler)
36.     batch_size = feedback.outputs[0].data.shape[0]
37.     outputs.append(feedback.outputs)
38.     new_rng_key, rng_key = jax.random.split(rng_key)
39.     cur_preds, _ = predict_fn(new_rng_key, feedback.features)
40.     preds.append(cur_preds)
41.     processed_samples += batch_size
42.     adjacency_batches.append(feedback[0][0][2].data)
43.     source_batches.append(np.argmax(feedback[0][0][1].data, axis=1))
44. 
45.   outputs = concat_tree(outputs, axis=0)
46.   adjacency = concat_tree(adjacency_batches, axis=0)
47.   source_nodes = concat_tree(source_batches, axis=0)
48.   preds = concat_tree(preds, axis=0)
49.   out = clrs.evaluate(outputs, preds)
50. 
51.   categorical = evaluate_sampling_pair(
52.       model_sample_fn=lambda data: bfs_sampling.sample_bfs_categorical(data),
53.       true_sample_fn=lambda data: bfs_sampling.sample_bfs_categorical(data),
54.       model_input=[preds],
55.       true_input=outputs,
56.       adjacency=adjacency,
57.       source_nodes=source_nodes,
58.       validate_fn=bfs_validation.check_valid_bfs_tree,
59.   )
60.   random_sampling = evaluate_sampling_pair(
61.       model_sample_fn=lambda data: dfs_sampling.sample_random_list(data),
62.       true_sample_fn=lambda data: dfs_sampling.sample_random_list(data),
63.       model_input=[preds],
64.       true_input=outputs,
65.       adjacency=adjacency,
66.       source_nodes=source_nodes,
67.       validate_fn=bfs_validation.check_valid_bfs_tree,
68.   )
69.   prim = evaluate_sampling_pair(
70.       model_sample_fn=lambda data, s: bfs_sampling.sample_bfs_prim(data, s),
71.       true_sample_fn=lambda data, s: bfs_sampling.sample_bfs_prim(data, s),
72.       model_input=[preds],
73.       true_input=outputs,
74.       adjacency=adjacency,
75.       source_nodes=source_nodes,
76.       validate_fn=bfs_validation.check_valid_bfs_tree,
77.       s=source_nodes,
78.   )
79.   beam = evaluate_sampling_pair(
80.       model_sample_fn=lambda data, s: bfs_sampling.sample_bfs_beam(
81.           data, s, beam_width=3),
82.       true_sample_fn=lambda data, s: bfs_sampling.sample_bfs_beam(
83.           data, s, beam_width=3),
84.       model_input=[preds],
85.       true_input=outputs,
86.       adjacency=adjacency,
87.       source_nodes=source_nodes,
88.       validate_fn=bfs_validation.check_valid_bfs_tree,
89.       s=source_nodes,
90.   )
91. 
92.   result_dict = reports.build_bfs_result_dict(
93.       adjacency_flat=[i.flatten() for i in adjacency],
94.       source_nodes=source_nodes,
95.       categorical=categorical,
96.       random_sampling=random_sampling,
97.       prim=prim,
98.       beam=beam,
99.   )
100.   save_results_fn(result_dict, f"{filename}_BFS")
101. 
102.   if extras:
103.     out.update(copy.deepcopy(extras))
104.   return {k: _unpack(v) for k, v in out.items()}
105. 
106. 
107. def _unpack(v):
108.   try:
109.     return v.item()
110.   except (AttributeError, ValueError):
111.     return v
112. 
113.

8. def evaluate_sampling_pair(

13.     adjacency,

19.   true_trees = true_sample_fn(true_input, **kwargs)

31.       "model_mask": model_mask,

20. 
21. *Evaluate*
22. - Run `results/viz.ipynb` all the way through
23. 
24. 
25. ## Files that matter
26. - `clrs/examples/run.py` lets you train the models and generate results `.csv`s, when run with correct flags
27. - `clrs/examples/log_experiments.py` gets called by `run.py` and produces the `.csv` files
28. - `results/viz.ipynb` lets you recreate the figures from `.csv` files
29. - `clrs/_src/validate_distributions.py` does appendix stuff
30. 
31. Tips navigating CLRS
32. - Use an editor that quickly lets you find a function's definition with a keyboard shortcut, otherwise tracing prediction through baselines, nets, etc... is time consuming
33. - `run.py` sets up `samplers` which make problem instances (e.g. graphs for DFS).
34.   - problem instances live inside named tuples:
35.     - inputs in `feedback.features.inputs` (e.g. Adjacency matrix and Start node)
36.     - labels inside `feedback.features.outputs` (e.g. Correct DFS tree)
37.     - hints inside `feedback.features.hints` 
38. 
39. - Networks predict on `feedback.features.inputs`
40. - Loss is computed by comparing NN output to `feedback.features.outputs`
41. 
42. 
43. ---
44. 
45. *note labels typically come from classical implementations of algorithms (e.g. `dfs` inside `clrs/_src/algorithms/graphs.py`). For solution distributions, we adaped `graphs.py` to average multiple runs of each algorithm and use that empirical distribution as training label*
46. 
47. 
48. ----
49. 
50. # The CLRS Algorithmic Reasoning Benchmark
51. 
52. Learning representations of algorithms is an emerging area of machine learning,
53. seeking to bridge concepts from neural networks with classical algorithms. The
54. CLRS Algorithmic Reasoning Benchmark (CLRS) consolidates and extends previous
55. work toward evaluation algorithmic reasoning by providing a suite of
56. implementations of classical algorithms. These algorithms have been selected
57. from the third edition of the standard *Introduction to Algorithms* by Cormen,
58. Leiserson, Rivest and Stein.
59. 
60. ## Getting started
61. 
62. The CLRS Algorithmic Reasoning Benchmark can be installed with pip, either from
63. PyPI:
64. 
65. ```shell
66. pip install dm-clrs
67. ```
68. 
69. or directly from GitHub (updated more frequently):
70.
````

1. """Objective helpers for multi-solution losses."""

3. import jax

6. from clrs._src.multi_sol.training.output_head import multisol_softmax

9. def kl_divergence_truth_pred(truth, pred_logits, epsilon: float = 1e-8):
10.   """KL divergence utility matching existing MULT_SOL training behavior."""
11.   return jnp.mean(
12.       kl_divergence_truth_pred_elementwise(
13.           truth=truth,
14.           pred_logits=pred_logits,
15.           epsilon=epsilon))
16. 
17. 
18. def kl_divergence_truth_pred_elementwise(
19.     truth,
20.     pred_logits,
21.     epsilon: float = 1e-8,
22. ):
23.   """Elementwise KL(truth || pred_probs), shape-compatible with `truth`."""
24.   probs = multisol_softmax(pred_logits, axis=-1)
25.   return jax.scipy.special.kl_div(truth, probs + epsilon)
26.

36. def log_sinkhorn(x: _Array, steps: int, temperature: float, zero_diagonal: bool,
37.                  noise_rng_key: Optional[_Array]) -> _Array:
38.   """Sinkhorn operator in log space, to postprocess permutation pointer logits.
39. 
40.   Args:
41.     x: input of shape [..., n, n], a batch of square matrices.
42.     steps: number of iterations.
43.     temperature: temperature parameter (as temperature approaches zero, the
44.       output approaches a permutation matrix).
45.     zero_diagonal: whether to force the diagonal logits towards -inf.
46.     noise_rng_key: key to add Gumbel noise.
47. 
48.   Returns:
49.     Elementwise logarithm of a doubly-stochastic matrix (a matrix with
50.     non-negative elements whose rows and columns sum to 1).
51.   """
52.   assert x.ndim >= 2
53.   assert x.shape[-1] == x.shape[-2]
54.   if noise_rng_key is not None:
55.     # Add standard Gumbel noise (see https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.08665)
56.     noise = -jnp.log(-jnp.log(jax.random.uniform(noise_rng_key,
57.                                                  x.shape) + 1e-12) + 1e-12)
58.     x = x + noise
59.   x /= temperature
60.   if zero_diagonal:
61.     x = x - 1e6 * jnp.eye(x.shape[-1])
62.   for _ in range(steps):
63.     x = jax.nn.log_softmax(x, axis=-1)
64.     x = jax.nn.log_softmax(x, axis=-2)
65.   return x
66.

68. def construct_decoders(loc: str, t: str, hidden_dim: int, nb_dims: int,
69.                        name: str):
70.   """Constructs decoders."""
71.   linear = functools.partial(hk.Linear, name=f"{name}_dec_linear")
72.   if loc == _Location.NODE:
73.     # Node decoders.
74.     if t in [_Type.SCALAR, _Type.MASK, _Type.MASK_ONE]:
75.       decoders = (linear(1),)
76.     elif t == _Type.CATEGORICAL:
77.       decoders = (linear(nb_dims),)
78.     elif t in [_Type.POINTER, _Type.PERMUTATION_POINTER]:
79.       decoders = (linear(hidden_dim), linear(hidden_dim), linear(hidden_dim),
80.                   linear(1))
81.     elif t == _Type.MULT_SOL:
82.       decoders = (linear(hidden_dim), linear(hidden_dim), linear(hidden_dim),
83.                   linear(1)) #FIXME
84.     # TODO make sure no negative preds!
85.     # if doesn't work, try 4 linear of hidden_dimension, use instead of maximum
86.     else:
87.       raise ValueError(f"Invalid Type {t}")
88. 
89.   elif loc == _Location.EDGE:
90.     # Edge decoders.
91.     if t in [_Type.SCALAR, _Type.MASK, _Type.MASK_ONE]:
92.       decoders = (linear(1), linear(1), linear(1))
93.     elif t == _Type.CATEGORICAL:
94.       decoders = (linear(nb_dims), linear(nb_dims), linear(nb_dims))
95.     elif t == _Type.POINTER:
96.       decoders = (linear(hidden_dim), linear(hidden_dim),
97.                   linear(hidden_dim), linear(hidden_dim), linear(1))
98.     else:
99.       raise ValueError(f"Invalid Type {t}")
100. 
101.   elif loc == _Location.GRAPH:
102.     # Graph decoders.
103.     if t in [_Type.SCALAR, _Type.MASK, _Type.MASK_ONE]:
104.       decoders = (linear(1), linear(1))
105.     elif t == _Type.CATEGORICAL:
106.       decoders = (linear(nb_dims), linear(nb_dims))
107.     elif t == _Type.POINTER:
108.       decoders = (linear(1), linear(1),
109.                   linear(1))
110.     else:

112. 
113.   else:

130. def postprocess(spec: _Spec, preds: Dict[str, _Array],
131.                 sinkhorn_temperature: float,
132.                 sinkhorn_steps: int,
133.                 hard: bool) -> Dict[str, _DataPoint]:
134.   """Postprocesses decoder output.
135. 
136.   This is done on outputs in order to score performance, and on hints in
137.   order to score them but also in order to feed them back to the model.
138.   At scoring time, the postprocessing mode is "hard", logits will be
139.   arg-maxed and masks will be thresholded. However, for the case of the hints
140.   that are fed back in the model, the postprocessing can be hard or soft,
141.   depending on whether we want to let gradients flow through them or not.
142. 
143.   Args:
144.     spec: The spec of the algorithm whose outputs/hints we are postprocessing.
145.     preds: Output and/or hint predictions, as produced by decoders.
146.     sinkhorn_temperature: Parameter for the sinkhorn operator on permutation
147.       pointers.
148.     sinkhorn_steps: Parameter for the sinkhorn operator on permutation
149.       pointers.
150.     hard: whether to do hard postprocessing, which involves argmax for
151.       MASK_ONE, CATEGORICAL and POINTERS, thresholding for MASK, and stop
152.       gradient through for SCALAR. If False, soft postprocessing will be used,
153.       with softmax, sigmoid and gradients allowed.
154.   Returns:
155.     The postprocessed `preds`. In "soft" post-processing, POINTER types will
156.     change to SOFT_POINTER, so encoders know they do not need to be
157.     pre-processed before feeding them back in.
158.   """
159.   result = {}
160.   for name in preds.keys():
161.     _, loc, t = spec[name]
162.     new_t = t
163.     data = preds[name]
164.     if t == _Type.SCALAR:
165.       if hard:
166.         data = jax.lax.stop_gradient(data)
167.     elif t == _Type.MASK:
168.       if hard:
169.         data = (data > 0.0) * 1.0
170.       else:
171.         data = jax.nn.sigmoid(data)
172.     elif t in [_Type.MASK_ONE, _Type.CATEGORICAL]:
173.       cat_size = data.shape[-1]
174.       if hard:
175.         best = jnp.argmax(data, -1)
176.         data = hk.one_hot(best, cat_size)
177.       else:
178.         data = jax.nn.softmax(data, axis=-1)
179.     elif t == _Type.POINTER:
180.       if hard:
181.         #print('decoders.py, postprocess: ', data)
182.         data = jnp.argmax(data, -1).astype(float)
183.       else:
184.         data = jax.nn.softmax(data, -1)
185.         new_t = _Type.SOFT_POINTER
186.     elif t == _Type.PERMUTATION_POINTER:
187.       # Convert the matrix of logits to a doubly stochastic matrix.
188.       data = log_sinkhorn(
189.           x=data,
190.           steps=sinkhorn_steps,
191.           temperature=sinkhorn_temperature,
192.           zero_diagonal=True,
193.           noise_rng_key=None)
194.       data = jnp.exp(data)
195.       if hard:
196.         data = jax.nn.one_hot(jnp.argmax(data, axis=-1), data.shape[-1])
197.     elif t == _Type.MULT_SOL:
198.       data = multisol_output_head.multisol_softmax(data, axis=-1)
199.     else:
200.       raise ValueError("Invalid type")
201.     result[name] = probing.DataPoint(
202.         name=name, location=loc, type_=new_t, data=data)
203. 
204.   return result
205.

207. def decode_fts(
208.     decoders,
209.     spec: _Spec,
210.     h_t: _Array,
211.     adj_mat: _Array,
212.     edge_fts: _Array,
213.     graph_fts: _Array,
214.     inf_bias: bool,
215.     inf_bias_edge: bool,
216.     repred: bool,
217. ):
218.   """Decodes node, edge and graph features."""
219.   output_preds = {}
220.   hint_preds = {}
221. 
222.   for name in decoders:
223.     decoder = decoders[name]
224.     stage, loc, t = spec[name]
225. 
226.     if loc == _Location.NODE:
227.       preds = _decode_node_fts(decoder, t, h_t, edge_fts, adj_mat,
228.                                inf_bias, repred)
229.     elif loc == _Location.EDGE:
230.       preds = _decode_edge_fts(decoder, t, h_t, edge_fts, adj_mat,
231.                                inf_bias_edge)
232.     elif loc == _Location.GRAPH:
233.       preds = _decode_graph_fts(decoder, t, h_t, graph_fts)
234.     else:
235.       raise ValueError("Invalid output type")
236. 
237.     if stage == _Stage.OUTPUT:
238.       output_preds[name] = preds
239.     elif stage == _Stage.HINT:
240.       hint_preds[name] = preds
241.     else:
242.       raise ValueError(f"Found unexpected decoder {name}")
243. 
244.   return hint_preds, output_preds
245.

247. def _decode_node_fts(decoders, t: str, h_t: _Array, edge_fts: _Array,
248.                      adj_mat: _Array, inf_bias: bool, repred: bool) -> _Array:
249.   """Decodes node features."""
250. 
251.   if t in [_Type.SCALAR, _Type.MASK, _Type.MASK_ONE]:
252.     preds = jnp.squeeze(decoders[0](h_t), -1)
253.   elif t == _Type.CATEGORICAL:
254.     preds = decoders[0](h_t)
255.   elif t == _Type.MULT_SOL:
256.     # breakpoint() weird! if you have this breakpoint and continue, you get an error. But run without, no error arises
257.     p_1 = decoders[0](h_t)  # from vector:  shape [batch,nodes,hidden]
258.     p_2 = decoders[1](h_t)  # to vector:  shape [batch,nodes,hidden]
259.     p_3 = decoders[2](edge_fts)  # edge features: [batch,nodes,nodes,hidden]
260. 
261.     p_e = jnp.expand_dims(p_2, -2) + p_3  # [batch,nodes,1,hidden] summed with [batch,nodes,nodes,hidden]
262.     # to_i  + edge_ij: [batch,nodes_i,nodes_j,hidden]
263. 
264.     p_m = jnp.maximum(jnp.expand_dims(p_1, -2),  # [batch,nodes_i,1,hidden] -> [batch,nodes_i,nodes_i,hidden]
265.                       jnp.transpose(p_e, (0, 2, 1, 3)))  # [batch, nodes_j, nodes_i, hidden]
266.     # p_m shape [batch, nodes_j, nodes_i, hidden]
267.     # computed elementwise max of (to_i + edge_ij, from_i)
268. 
269.     preds = jnp.squeeze(decoders[3](p_m), -1)  # cut out hidden dimension
270. 
271.     # in-case this doesn't work. instead of jnp.maximum, another decoder.
272.     # decoders.for
273. 
274.     if inf_bias:
275.       per_batch_min = jnp.min(preds, axis=range(1, preds.ndim), keepdims=True)
276.       preds = jnp.where(adj_mat > 0.5,
277.                         preds,
278.                         jnp.minimum(-1.0, per_batch_min - 1.0))
279.     if t == _Type.PERMUTATION_POINTER:
280.       if repred:  # testing or validation, no Gumbel noise
281.         preds = log_sinkhorn(
282.             x=preds, steps=10, temperature=0.1,
283.             zero_diagonal=True, noise_rng_key=None)
284.       else:  # training, add Gumbel noise
285.         preds = log_sinkhorn(
286.             x=preds, steps=10, temperature=0.1,
287.             zero_diagonal=True, noise_rng_key=hk.next_rng_key())
288.   elif t in [_Type.POINTER, _Type.PERMUTATION_POINTER]:
289.     p_1 = decoders[0](h_t) # from vector
290.     p_2 = decoders[1](h_t) # to vector  shape [batch,nodes,hidden]
291.     p_3 = decoders[2](edge_fts) # edge features [batch,nodes,nodes,hidden]
292. 
293.     p_e = jnp.expand_dims(p_2, -2) + p_3 # [batch,nodes,1,hidden] summed with [batch,nodes,nodes,hidden]
294.     # to_i  + edge_ij: [batch,nodes_i,nodes_j,hidden]
295.     #jax.debug.print("preds before max: {}", p_e)
296.     p_m = jnp.maximum(jnp.expand_dims(p_1, -2), # [batch,nodes_i,1,hidden] -> [batch,nodes_i,nodes_i,hidden]
297.                       jnp.transpose(p_e, (0, 2, 1, 3))) # [batch, nodes_j, nodes_i, hidden]
298.     #p_m shape [batch, nodes_j, nodes_i, hidden]
299.     # computed elementwise max of (to_i + edge_ij, from_i)
300. 
301.     preds = jnp.squeeze(decoders[3](p_m), -1) # cut out hidden dimension
302.     #to = to.max(from+edge)
303.     #jax.debug.print("preds post-max: {}", preds)
304.     #breakpoint()
305.     #decoders.for
306. 
307.     if inf_bias:
308.       per_batch_min = jnp.min(preds, axis=range(1, preds.ndim), keepdims=True)
309.       preds = jnp.where(adj_mat > 0.5,
310.                         preds,
311.                         jnp.minimum(-1.0, per_batch_min - 1.0))
312.     if t == _Type.PERMUTATION_POINTER:
313.       if repred:  # testing or validation, no Gumbel noise
314.         preds = log_sinkhorn(
315.             x=preds, steps=10, temperature=0.1,
316.             zero_diagonal=True, noise_rng_key=None)
317.       else:  # training, add Gumbel noise
318.         preds = log_sinkhorn(
319.             x=preds, steps=10, temperature=0.1,
320.             zero_diagonal=True, noise_rng_key=hk.next_rng_key())
321.   else:
322.     raise ValueError("Invalid output type")
323. 
324.   return preds
325.

327. def _decode_edge_fts(decoders, t: str, h_t: _Array, edge_fts: _Array,
328.                      adj_mat: _Array, inf_bias_edge: bool) -> _Array:
329.   """Decodes edge features."""
330. 
331.   pred_1 = decoders[0](h_t)
332.   pred_2 = decoders[1](h_t)
333.   pred_e = decoders[2](edge_fts)
334.   pred = (jnp.expand_dims(pred_1, -2) + jnp.expand_dims(pred_2, -3) + pred_e)
335.   if t in [_Type.SCALAR, _Type.MASK, _Type.MASK_ONE]:
336.     preds = jnp.squeeze(pred, -1)
337.   elif t == _Type.CATEGORICAL:
338.     preds = pred
339.   elif t == _Type.POINTER:
340.     pred_2 = decoders[3](h_t)
341. 
342.     p_m = jnp.maximum(jnp.expand_dims(pred, -2),
343.                       jnp.expand_dims(
344.                           jnp.expand_dims(pred_2, -3), -3))
345. 
346.     preds = jnp.squeeze(decoders[4](p_m), -1)
347.   else:
348.     raise ValueError("Invalid output type")
349.   if inf_bias_edge and t in [_Type.MASK, _Type.MASK_ONE]:
350.     per_batch_min = jnp.min(preds, axis=range(1, preds.ndim), keepdims=True)
351.     preds = jnp.where(adj_mat > 0.5,
352.                       preds,
353.                       jnp.minimum(-1.0, per_batch_min - 1.0))
354. 
355.   return preds
356. 
357. 
358. def _decode_graph_fts(decoders, t: str, h_t: _Array,
359.                       graph_fts: _Array) -> _Array:
360.   """Decodes graph features."""
361. 
362.   gr_emb = jnp.max(h_t, axis=-2)
363.   pred_n = decoders[0](gr_emb)
364.   pred_g = decoders[1](graph_fts)
365.   pred = pred_n + pred_g
366.   if t in [_Type.SCALAR, _Type.MASK, _Type.MASK_ONE]:
367.     preds = jnp.squeeze(pred, -1)
368.   elif t == _Type.CATEGORICAL:
369.     preds = pred
370.   elif t == _Type.POINTER:
371.     pred_2 = decoders[2](h_t)
372.     ptr_p = jnp.expand_dims(pred, 1) + jnp.transpose(pred_2, (0, 2, 1))
373.     preds = jnp.squeeze(ptr_p, 1)
374.   else:
375.     raise ValueError("Invalid output type")
376. 
377.   return preds
378. 
379. 
380. def maybe_decode_diffs(
381.     diff_decoders,
382.     h_t: _Array,
383.     edge_fts: _Array,
384.     graph_fts: _Array,
385.     decode_diffs: bool,
386. ) -> Optional[Dict[str, _Array]]:
387.   """Optionally decodes node, edge and graph diffs."""
388. 
389.   if decode_diffs:
390.     preds = {}
391.     node = _Location.NODE
392.     edge = _Location.EDGE
393.     graph = _Location.GRAPH
394.     preds[node] = _decode_node_diffs(diff_decoders[node], h_t)
395.     preds[edge] = _decode_edge_diffs(diff_decoders[edge], h_t, edge_fts)
396.     preds[graph] = _decode_graph_diffs(diff_decoders[graph], h_t, graph_fts)
397. 
398.   else:
399.     preds = None
400. 
401.   return preds
402. 
403. 
404. def _decode_node_diffs(decoders, h_t: _Array) -> _Array:
405.   """Decodes node diffs."""
406.   return jnp.squeeze(decoders(h_t), -1)
407. 
408. 
409. def _decode_edge_diffs(decoders, h_t: _Array, edge_fts: _Array) -> _Array:
410.   """Decodes edge diffs."""
411. 
412.   e_pred_1 = decoders[0](h_t)
413.   e_pred_2 = decoders[1](h_t)
414.   e_pred_e = decoders[2](edge_fts)
415.   preds = jnp.squeeze(
416.       jnp.expand_dims(e_pred_1, -1) + jnp.expand_dims(e_pred_2, -2) + e_pred_e,
417.       -1,
418.   )
419. 
420.   return preds
421. 
422. 
423. def _decode_graph_diffs(decoders, h_t: _Array, graph_fts: _Array) -> _Array:
424.   """Decodes graph diffs."""
425. 
426.   gr_emb = jnp.max(h_t, axis=-2)
427.   g_pred_n = decoders[0](gr_emb)
428.   g_pred_g = decoders[1](graph_fts)
429.   preds = jnp.squeeze(g_pred_n + g_pred_g, -1)
430. 
431.   return preds
432.

39. def _expand_to(x: _Array, y: _Array) -> _Array:
40.   while len(y.shape) > len(x.shape):
41.     x = jnp.expand_dims(x, -1)
42.   return x

46.   return jnp.broadcast_to(_expand_to(x, y), y.shape)

49. def output_loss_chunked(truth: _DataPoint, pred: _Array,
50.                         is_last: _Array, nb_nodes: int) -> float:
51.   """Output loss for time-chunked training."""
52. 
53.   mask = None
54. 
55.   if truth.type_ == _Type.SCALAR:
56.     loss = (pred - truth.data)**2
57. 
58.   elif truth.type_ == _Type.MASK:
59.     loss = (
60.         jnp.maximum(pred, 0) - pred * truth.data +
61.         jnp.log1p(jnp.exp(-jnp.abs(pred))))
62.     mask = (truth.data != _OutputClass.MASKED)
63. 
64.   elif truth.type_ in [_Type.MASK_ONE, _Type.CATEGORICAL]:
65.     mask = jnp.any(truth.data == _OutputClass.POSITIVE, axis=-1)
66.     masked_truth = truth.data * (truth.data != _OutputClass.MASKED).astype(
67.         jnp.float32)
68.     loss = -jnp.sum(masked_truth * jax.nn.log_softmax(pred), axis=-1)
69. 
70.   elif truth.type_ == _Type.POINTER:
71.     loss = -jnp.sum(
72.         hk.one_hot(truth.data, nb_nodes) * jax.nn.log_softmax(pred), axis=-1)
73. 
74.   elif truth.type_ == _Type.PERMUTATION_POINTER:
75.     # Predictions are NxN logits aiming to represent a doubly stochastic matrix.
76.     # Compute the cross entropy between doubly stochastic pred and truth_data
77.     loss = -jnp.sum(truth.data * pred, axis=-1)
78. 
79.   elif truth.type_ == _Type.MULT_SOL:
80.     # Predictions are NxN logits. Compute row-wise KL(truth || pred_probs).
81.     loss = multisol_objectives.kl_divergence_truth_pred_elementwise(
82.         truth.data, pred)
83. 
84.   if mask is not None:
85.     mask = mask * _expand_and_broadcast_to(is_last, loss)
86.   else:
87.     mask = _expand_and_broadcast_to(is_last, loss)
88.   total_mask = jnp.maximum(jnp.sum(mask), EPS)
89.   return jnp.sum(jnp.where(mask, loss, 0.0)) / total_mask  # pytype: disable=bad-return-type  # jnp-type
90. 
91. 
92. def output_loss(truth: _DataPoint, pred: _Array, nb_nodes: int) -> float:
93.   """Output loss for full-sample training."""
94. 
95.   if truth.type_ == _Type.SCALAR:
96.     total_loss = jnp.mean((pred - truth.data)**2)
97. 
98.   elif truth.type_ == _Type.MASK:
99.     loss = (
100.         jnp.maximum(pred, 0) - pred * truth.data +
101.         jnp.log1p(jnp.exp(-jnp.abs(pred))))
102.     mask = (truth.data != _OutputClass.MASKED).astype(jnp.float32)
103.     total_loss = jnp.sum(loss * mask) / jnp.sum(mask)
104. 
105.   elif truth.type_ in [_Type.MASK_ONE, _Type.CATEGORICAL]:
106.     masked_truth = truth.data * (truth.data != _OutputClass.MASKED).astype(
107.         jnp.float32)
108.     total_loss = (-jnp.sum(masked_truth * jax.nn.log_softmax(pred)) /
109.                   jnp.sum(truth.data == _OutputClass.POSITIVE))
110. 
111.   elif truth.type_ == _Type.POINTER:
112.     total_loss = (
113.         jnp.mean(-jnp.sum(
114.             hk.one_hot(truth.data, nb_nodes) * jax.nn.log_softmax(pred),
115.             axis=-1)))
116. 
117.   elif truth.type_ == _Type.PERMUTATION_POINTER:
118.     # Predictions are NxN logits aiming to represent a doubly stochastic matrix.
119.     # Compute the cross entropy between doubly stochastic pred and truth_data
120.     total_loss = jnp.mean(-jnp.sum(truth.data * pred, axis=-1))
121. 
122.   elif truth.type_ == _Type.MULT_SOL:
123.     total_loss = multisol_objectives.kl_divergence_truth_pred(truth.data, pred)
124. 
125.   return total_loss  # pytype: disable=bad-return-type  # jnp-type
126. 
127. 
128. def hint_loss_chunked(
129.     truth: _DataPoint,
130.     pred: _Array,
131.     is_first: _Array,
132.     nb_nodes: int,
133. ):
134.   """Hint loss for time-chunked training."""
135.   loss, mask = _hint_loss(
136.       truth_data=truth.data,
137.       truth_type=truth.type_,
138.       pred=pred,
139.       nb_nodes=nb_nodes,
140.   )
141. 
142.   mask *= (1 - _expand_to(is_first, loss)).astype(jnp.float32)
143.   loss = jnp.sum(loss * mask) / jnp.maximum(jnp.sum(mask), EPS)
144.   return loss
145. 
146. 
147. def hint_loss(
148.     truth: _DataPoint,
149.     preds: List[_Array],
150.     lengths: _Array,
151.     nb_nodes: int,
152.     verbose: bool = False,
153. ):
154.   """Hint loss for full-sample training."""
155.   total_loss = 0.
156.   verbose_loss = {}
157.   length = truth.data.shape[0] - 1
158. 
159.   loss, mask = _hint_loss(
160.       truth_data=truth.data[1:],
161.       truth_type=truth.type_,
162.       pred=jnp.stack(preds),
163.       nb_nodes=nb_nodes,
164.   )
165.   mask *= _is_not_done_broadcast(lengths, jnp.arange(length)[:, None], loss)
166.   loss = jnp.sum(loss * mask) / jnp.maximum(jnp.sum(mask), EPS)
167.   if verbose:
168.     verbose_loss['loss_' + truth.name] = loss
169.   else:
170.     total_loss += loss
171. 
172.   return verbose_loss if verbose else total_loss
173. 
174. 
175. def _hint_loss(
176.     truth_data: _Array,
177.     truth_type: str,
178.     pred: _Array,
179.     nb_nodes: int,
180. ) -> Tuple[_Array, _Array]:
181.   """Hint loss helper."""
182.   mask = None
183.   if truth_type == _Type.SCALAR:
184.     loss = (pred - truth_data)**2
185. 
186.   elif truth_type == _Type.MASK:
187.     loss = (jnp.maximum(pred, 0) - pred * truth_data +
188.             jnp.log1p(jnp.exp(-jnp.abs(pred))))
189.     mask = (truth_data != _OutputClass.MASKED).astype(jnp.float32)  # pytype: disable=attribute-error  # numpy-scalars
190. 
191.   elif truth_type == _Type.MASK_ONE:
192.     loss = -jnp.sum(truth_data * jax.nn.log_softmax(pred), axis=-1,
193.                     keepdims=True)
194. 
195.   elif truth_type == _Type.CATEGORICAL:
196.     loss = -jnp.sum(truth_data * jax.nn.log_softmax(pred), axis=-1)
197.     mask = jnp.any(truth_data == _OutputClass.POSITIVE, axis=-1).astype(
198.         jnp.float32)
199. 
200.   elif truth_type == _Type.POINTER:
201.     loss = -jnp.sum(
202.         hk.one_hot(truth_data, nb_nodes) * jax.nn.log_softmax(pred),
203.         axis=-1)
204. 
205.   elif truth_type == _Type.PERMUTATION_POINTER:
206.     # Predictions are NxN logits aiming to represent a doubly stochastic matrix.
207.     # Compute the cross entropy between doubly stochastic pred and truth_data
208.     loss = -jnp.sum(truth_data * pred, axis=-1)
209. 
210.   elif truth_type == _Type.MULT_SOL:
211.     loss = multisol_objectives.kl_divergence_truth_pred_elementwise(
212.         truth_data, pred)
213. 
214.   if mask is None:
215.     mask = jnp.ones_like(loss)
216.   return loss, mask
217. 
218. 
219. def _is_not_done_broadcast(lengths, i, tensor):
220.   is_not_done = (lengths > i + 1) * 1.0
221.   while len(is_not_done.shape) < len(tensor.shape):  # pytype: disable=attribute-error  # numpy-scalars
222.     is_not_done = jnp.expand_dims(is_not_done, -1)
223.   return is_not_done
224.

26. _Array = chex.Array
27. Result = Dict[str, probing.DataPoint]

29. 
30. def fuse_perm_and_mask(perm: probing.DataPoint,
31.                        mask: probing.DataPoint) -> probing.DataPoint:
32.   """Replace permutation pointers active in the mask with self-pointers.
33. 
34.   Args:
35.     perm: a node permutation_pointer; data shape is expected to be
36.       [..., N, N], and ideally one-hot over the last two dimensions, although
37.       this method does not check for one-hotness.
38.     mask: a mask_one over nodes; data shape is expected to be
39.       [..., N], and ideally one-hot over the last dimension, although
40.       this method does not check for one-hotness.
41.   Returns:
42.     A node pointer with shape [..., N].
43.   """
44.   assert perm.type_ == specs.Type.PERMUTATION_POINTER
45.   assert perm.location == specs.Location.NODE
46.   assert mask.name == perm.name + '_mask'
47.   assert mask.type_ == specs.Type.MASK_ONE
48.   assert mask.location == specs.Location.NODE
49.   assert perm.data.shape[-1] == perm.data.shape[-2]
50.   assert perm.data.shape[:-1] == mask.data.shape
51.   data = np.where(mask.data > 0.5,
52.                   np.arange(perm.data.shape[-1]),  # self-pointers
53.                   np.argmax(perm.data, axis=-1))   # original pointers
54.   return probing.DataPoint(name=perm.name,
55.                            type_=specs.Type.POINTER,
56.                            location=perm.location,
57.                            data=data)
58. 
59. 
60. def _reduce_permutations_tuple(
61.     targets: Tuple[probing.DataPoint, ...]) -> Tuple[probing.DataPoint, ...]:
62.   """Reduce node pointer + mask_one permutation to just node pointer."""
63.   out_targets = []
64.   n_perms = 0
65.   i = 0
66.   while i < len(targets):
67.     truth = targets[i]
68.     #hi
69.     #print('in evalutation, truth=', truth)
70.     #print(truth.data)
71.     if truth.type_ != specs.Type.PERMUTATION_POINTER:
72.       out_targets.append(truth)
73.       i += 1
74.       continue
75.     truth_mask = targets[i + 1]
76.     out_targets.append(fuse_perm_and_mask(truth, truth_mask))
77.     i += 2
78.     n_perms += 1
79. 
80.   assert len(out_targets) == len(targets) - n_perms
81.   return tuple(out_targets)
82. 
83. 
84. def _reduce_permutations_dict(predictions: Result) -> Result:
85.   """Reduce node pointer + mask_one permutation to just node pointer."""
86.   out_preds = {}
87.   n_perms = 0
88.   for k, pred in predictions.items():
89.     if (k.endswith('_mask') and k[:-5] in predictions and
90.         predictions[k[:-5]].type_ == specs.Type.PERMUTATION_POINTER):
91.       # This mask will be processed with its associated permutation datapoint
92.       continue
93.     if pred.type_ != specs.Type.PERMUTATION_POINTER:
94.       out_preds[k] = pred
95.       continue
96.     pred_mask = predictions[k + '_mask']
97.     out_preds[k] = fuse_perm_and_mask(pred, pred_mask)
98.     n_perms += 1
99. 
100.   assert len(out_preds) == len(predictions) - n_perms
101.   return out_preds
102. 
103. 
104. def evaluate_hints(
105.     hints: Tuple[probing.DataPoint, ...],
106.     lengths: _Array,
107.     hint_preds: List[Result],
108. ) -> Dict[str, _Array]:
109.   """Evaluate hint predictions."""
110.   evals = {}
111.   hints = _reduce_permutations_tuple(hints)
112.   hint_preds = [_reduce_permutations_dict(h) for h in hint_preds]
113.   for truth in hints:
114.     assert truth.name in hint_preds[0]
115.     eval_along_time = [_evaluate(truth, p[truth.name],
116.                                  idx=i+1, lengths=lengths)
117.                        for (i, p) in enumerate(hint_preds)]
118.     evals[truth.name] = np.sum(
119.         [x * np.sum(i+1 < lengths)
120.          for i, x in enumerate(eval_along_time)]) / np.sum(lengths - 1)
121.     evals[truth.name + '_along_time'] = np.array(eval_along_time)
122. 
123.   # Unlike outputs, the hints sometimes include scalars, which don't have
124.   # a meaningful eval score. So we don't compute a global 'hint score' as we
125.   # do for outputs.
126.   return evals
127. 
128. 
129. def evaluate(
130.     outputs: Tuple[probing.DataPoint, ...],
131.     predictions: Result,
132. ) -> Dict[str, float]:
133.   """Evaluate output predictions."""
134.   evals = {}
135.   #print('in evaluate method, outputs=', outputs)
136.   outputs = _reduce_permutations_tuple(outputs)
137.   #print('in evaluate method, predictions=', predictions)
138.   #print(predictions[0].data)
139.   predictions = _reduce_permutations_dict(predictions)
140.   for truth in outputs:
141.     assert truth.name in predictions
142.     pred = predictions[truth.name]
143.     evals[truth.name] = _evaluate(truth, pred)
144.     #breakpoint()
145.   # Return a single scalar score that is the mean of all output scores.
146.   evals['score'] = sum([v.item() for v in evals.values()]) / len(evals)
147.   return evals
148. 
149. 
150. def _evaluate(truth, pred, idx=None, lengths=None):
151.   """Evaluate single prediction of hint or output."""
152.   #breakpoint()
153.   assert pred.name == truth.name
154.   assert pred.location == truth.location
155.   assert pred.type_ == truth.type_
156. 
157.   if truth.type_ not in _EVAL_FN:
158.     raise ValueError('Invalid type')
159.   truth_data = truth.data
160.   pred_data = pred.data
161.   if idx is not None:
162.     if np.all(idx >= lengths):
163.       return 0.
164.     truth_data = truth_data[idx][idx < lengths]
165.     #print('truth_data: {}', truth_data)
166.     pred_data = pred_data[idx < lengths]
167.   #print('getting here?')
168.   #breakpoint()
169.   return _EVAL_FN[truth.type_](pred_data, truth_data)
170. 
171. 
172. def _eval_one(pred, truth):
173.   mask = np.all(truth != specs.OutputClass.MASKED, axis=-1)
174.   return np.sum(
175.       (np.argmax(pred, -1) == np.argmax(truth, -1)) * mask) / np.sum(mask)
176. 
177. 
178. def _mask_fn(pred, truth):
179.   """Evaluate outputs of type MASK, and account for any class imbalance."""
180.   mask = (truth != specs.OutputClass.MASKED).astype(np.float32)
181. 
182.   # Use F1 score for the masked outputs to address any imbalance
183.   tp = np.sum((((pred > 0.5) * (truth > 0.5)) * 1.0) * mask)
184.   fp = np.sum((((pred > 0.5) * (truth < 0.5)) * 1.0) * mask)
185.   fn = np.sum((((pred < 0.5) * (truth > 0.5)) * 1.0) * mask)
186. 
187.   # Protect against division by zero
188.   if tp + fp > 0:
189.     precision = tp / (tp + fp)
190.   else:
191.     precision = np.float32(1.0)
192.   if tp + fn > 0:
193.     recall = tp / (tp + fn)
194.   else:
195.     recall = np.float32(1.0)
196. 
197.   if precision + recall > 0.0:
198.     f_1 = 2.0 * precision * recall / (precision + recall)
199.   else:
200.     f_1 = np.float32(0.0)
201. 
202.   return f_1
203. 
204. _EVAL_FN = {
205.     specs.Type.SCALAR:
206.         lambda pred, truth: np.mean((pred - truth)**2),
207.     specs.Type.MASK: _mask_fn,
208.     specs.Type.MASK_ONE:
209.         _eval_one,
210.     specs.Type.CATEGORICAL:
211.         _eval_one,
212.     specs.Type.POINTER:
213.         lambda pred, truth: np.mean((pred == truth) * 1.0),
214.     specs.Type.MULT_SOL:
215.         multisol_metrics.multisol_score,
216. }
217.

137.                                                                                            probMatrices = outputs, method="beam")

142.     ########
143.     model_sample_argmax = dfs_sampling.sample_argmax([preds]) # doesn't use A or s
144.     true_sample_argmax = dfs_sampling.sample_argmax(outputs)
145. 
146.     model_argmax_truthmask = [check_graphs.check_valid_BFpaths(As[i], source_nodes[i], model_sample_argmax[i]) for i in
147.                             range(len(model_sample_argmax))]
148.     correctness_model_argmax = sum(model_argmax_truthmask) / len(model_argmax_truthmask)
149.

151.                            range(len(model_sample_random))]
152.     correctness_true_argmax = sum(true_argmax_truthmask) / len(true_argmax_truthmask)
153.

158.     model_sample_greedy = sample_greedysearch(As, source_nodes, [preds])
159.     true_sample_greedy = sample_greedysearch(As, source_nodes, outputs)
160. 
161.     model_greedy_truthmask = [check_graphs.check_valid_BFpaths(As[i], source_nodes[i], model_sample_greedy[i]) for i in

164.

166.                            range(len(model_sample_random))]

168. 
169.     model_greedy_uniques, model_greedy_valids_uniques, model_greedy_valids = check_uniqueness_bf(As = As, source_nodes = source_nodes,
170.         probMatrices=[preds], method = "greedy")
171.     true_greedy_uniques, true_greedy_valids_uniques, true_greedy_valids = check_uniqueness_bf(As = As, source_nodes = source_nodes,
172.         probMatrices=outputs, method = "greedy")
173.

249. def BFS_multi_collect_and_eval(sampler, predict_fn, sample_count, rng_key, extras,

268. def DFS_collect_and_eval(sampler, predict_fn, sample_count, rng_key, extras, filename = 'dfs_accuracy', vd_flag=False, NSE = 100):
269.     """Collect batch of output preds and evaluate them."""
270.     processed_samples = 0
271.     preds = []
272.     outputs = []
273.     As = []
274.     while processed_samples < sample_count:
275.         feedback = next(sampler)
276.         batch_size = feedback.outputs[0].data.shape[0]
277.         outputs.append(feedback.outputs)
278.         new_rng_key, rng_key = jax.random.split(rng_key)
279.         cur_preds, _ = predict_fn(new_rng_key, feedback.features)
280.         preds.append(cur_preds)
281.         processed_samples += batch_size
282.         As.append(feedback[0][0][1].data)
283.     outputs = _concat(outputs, axis=0)
284.     As = _concat(As, axis=0) # concatenate batches
285.     #breakpoint()
286. 
287.     if vd_flag:
288.         print('log_exp.py, vd_flag working')
289.         print('truncating DFS_collect_and_eval to 10 graphs')
290.         payload = build_dfs_validation_payload(
291.             adjacency=As,
292.             outputs=outputs,
293.             preds=preds,
294.         )
295.         dataframes, df = generate_validation_dataframes(
296.             payload=payload,
297.             nse=NSE,
298.             mode='DFS',
299.         )
300.         #breakpoint()
301.         plot_n_unique_by_n_extracted_dfs(dataframes, len(As[0]))
302. 
303.         # plot_edge_reuse_matrix_list_median(df, len(As[0]))
304.         # breakpoint()
305.         plot_edge_reuse_matrix_list_mean_dfs(df, payload.graph_size)
306.         line_plot_dfs(df, payload.graph_size)
307. 
308.     ### We need preds and A. We want to
309.     # 1. Sample from preds a candidate tree
310.     # 2. run check_graphs on candidate tree (using A as groundtruth)
311.     # 3. Collect validity result into a dataframe.
312. 
313.     t1 = time.time()
314.     ##### RANDOM
315.     model_sample_random = dfs_sampling.sample_random_list(preds)
316.     true_sample_random = dfs_sampling.sample_random_list(outputs)
317. 
318.     model_random_truthmask = [dfs_verification_tester.dfsverify(As[i], model_sample_random[i]) for i in range(len(model_sample_random))]
319.     correctness_model_random = sum(model_random_truthmask) / len(model_random_truthmask)
320. 
321.     true_random_truthmask = [dfs_verification_tester.dfsverify(As[i], true_sample_random[i]) for i in range(len(true_sample_random))]
322.     correctness_true_random = sum(true_random_truthmask) / len(true_random_truthmask)
323. 
324.     t2 = time.time()
325.     print('random checking in (seconds)', t2-t1)
326.     ##### ARGMAX
327.     ## remember to convert from jax arrays to lists for easy subsequent methods using .tolist()
328.     model_sample_argmax = dfs_sampling.sample_argmax_listofdict(preds)
329.     true_sample_argmax = dfs_sampling.sample_argmax_listofdatapoint(outputs)
330. 
331.     # compute the fraction of trees sampled from model output fulfilling the necessary conditions
332.     model_argmax_truthmask = [dfs_verification_tester.dfsverify(As[i], model_sample_argmax[i].tolist()) for i in range(len(model_sample_argmax))]
333.     correctness_model_argmax = sum(model_argmax_truthmask) / len(model_argmax_truthmask)
334. 
335.     # compute the fraction of trees sampled from true distributions fulfilling the necessary conditions
336.     true_argmax_truthmask = [dfs_verification_tester.dfsverify(As[i], true_sample_argmax[i].tolist()) for i in range(len(true_sample_argmax))]
337.     correctness_true_argmax = sum(true_argmax_truthmask) / len(true_argmax_truthmask)
338. 
339.     t3 = time.time()
340.     print('argmax checking in (seconds)', t3-t2)
341.     ##### UPWARDS
342.     model_sample_upwards = dfs_sampling.sample_upwards(preds)
343.     true_sample_upwards = dfs_sampling.sample_upwards(outputs)
344. 
345.     model_upwards_uniques, model_upwards_valids_uniques, model_upwards_valids = dfs_uniqueness_check.check_uniqueness_dfs(As, preds)
346.     true_upwards_uniques, true_upwards_valids_uniques, true_upwards_valids  = dfs_uniqueness_check.check_uniqueness_dfs(As, outputs)
347. 
348.     model_upwards_truthmask = [dfs_verification_tester.dfsverify(As[i], model_sample_upwards[i].astype(int)) for i in range(len(model_sample_upwards))]
349.     correctness_model_upwards = sum(model_upwards_truthmask) / len(model_upwards_truthmask)
350. 
351.     true_upwards_truthmask = [dfs_verification_tester.dfsverify(As[i], true_sample_upwards[i].astype(int)) for i in range(len(true_sample_upwards))]
352.     correctness_true_upwards = sum(true_upwards_truthmask) / len(true_upwards_truthmask)
353. 
354.     t4 = time.time()
355.     print('upwards checking in (seconds)', t4 - t3)
356.     ##### ALTUPWARDS
357.     model_sample_altUpwards = dfs_sampling.sample_altUpwards(preds)
358.     true_sample_altUpwards = dfs_sampling.sample_altUpwards(outputs)
359. 
360.     model_altupwards_uniques, model_altupwards_valids_uniques, model_altupwards_valids = dfs_uniqueness_check.check_uniqueness_dfs(As, preds, method="altupwards") #np.zeros(len(true_argmax_truthmask)),np.zeros(len(true_argmax_truthmask)),np.zeros(len(true_argmax_truthmask))
361.     true_altupwards_uniques, true_altupwards_valids_uniques, true_altupwards_valids  = dfs_uniqueness_check.check_uniqueness_dfs(As, outputs, method="altupwards") #np.zeros(len(true_argmax_truthmask)),np.zeros(len(true_argmax_truthmask)),np.zeros(len(true_argmax_truthmask))
362. 
363.     model_altUpwards_truthmask = [dfs_verification_tester.dfsverify(As[i], model_sample_altUpwards[i].astype(int)) for i in
364.                                   range(len(model_sample_altUpwards))]
365.     correctness_model_altUpwards = sum(model_altUpwards_truthmask) / len(model_altUpwards_truthmask)
366. 
367.     true_altUpwards_truthmask = [dfs_verification_tester.dfsverify(As[i], true_sample_altUpwards[i].astype(int)) for i in
368.                                  range(len(true_sample_altUpwards))]
369.     correctness_true_altUpwards = sum(true_altUpwards_truthmask) / len(true_altUpwards_truthmask)
370. 
371.     t5 = time.time()
372.     print('altUpwards checking in (seconds)', t5 - t4)
373.     #breakpoint()
374.     As = [i.flatten() for i in As]
375.     result_dict = {"As": As,
376.                  #
377.                  "Argmax_Model_Trees": model_sample_argmax,
378.                  "Argmax_True_Trees": true_sample_argmax,
379.                  #
380.                  "Argmax_Model_Mask": model_argmax_truthmask,
381.                  "Argmax_True_Mask": true_argmax_truthmask,
382.                  #
383.                  "Argmax_Model_Accuracy": correctness_model_argmax,
384.                  "Argmax_True_Accuracy": correctness_true_argmax,
385.                  #
386.                  ###
387.                  #
388.                  "Random_Model_Trees": model_sample_random,
389.                  "Random_True_Trees": true_sample_random,
390.                  #
391.                  "Random_Model_Mask": model_random_truthmask,
392.                  "Random_True_Mask": true_random_truthmask,
393.                  #
394.                  "Random_Model_Accuracy": correctness_model_random,
395.                  "Random_True_Accuracy": correctness_true_random,
396.                  #
397.                  ###
398.                  #
399.                  "Upwards_Model_Trees": model_sample_upwards,
400.                  "Upwards_True_Trees": true_sample_upwards,
401.                  #
402.                  "Upwards_Model_Mask": model_upwards_truthmask,
403.                  "Upwards_True_Mask": true_upwards_truthmask,
404.                  #
405.                  "Upwards_Model_Accuracy": correctness_model_upwards,
406.                  "Upwards_True_Accuracy": correctness_true_upwards,
407. 
408.                  "Upwards_Model_Uniques": model_upwards_uniques,
409.                  "Upwards_Model_Valids_Uniques" : model_upwards_valids_uniques,
410.                  "Upwards_Model_Valids": model_upwards_valids,
411. 
412.                  "Upwards_True_Uniques" : true_upwards_uniques,
413.                  "Upwards_True_Valids_Uniques": true_upwards_valids_uniques,
414.                  "Upwards_True_Valids" : true_upwards_valids,
415.                  #

1. """Objective helpers for multi-solution losses."""
2. 
3. import jax
4. import jax.numpy as jnp
5. 
6. from clrs._src.multi_sol.training.output_head import multisol_softmax
7. 
8. 
9. def kl_divergence_truth_pred(truth, pred_logits, epsilon: float = 1e-8):
10.   """KL divergence utility matching existing MULT_SOL training behavior."""
11.   return jnp.mean(
12.       kl_divergence_truth_pred_elementwise(
13.           truth=truth,
14.           pred_logits=pred_logits,
15.           epsilon=epsilon))
16. 
17. 
18. def kl_divergence_truth_pred_elementwise(
19.     truth,
20.     pred_logits,
21.     epsilon: float = 1e-8,
22. ):
23.   """Elementwise KL(truth || pred_probs), shape-compatible with `truth`."""
24.   probs = multisol_softmax(pred_logits, axis=-1)
25.   return jax.scipy.special.kl_div(truth, probs + epsilon)
26.

1. """BFS plugin wiring for modular multi-solution evaluation."""
2. 
3. import copy
4. from typing import Dict
5. 
6. import clrs
7. import jax
8. import numpy as np
9. 
10. from clrs._src import dfs_sampling
11. from clrs._src.multi_sol.data.adapters import concat_tree
12. from clrs._src.multi_sol.evaluation import reports
13. from clrs._src.multi_sol.evaluation.runners import evaluate_sampling_pair
14. from clrs._src.multi_sol.sampling import bfs as bfs_sampling
15. from clrs._src.multi_sol.validation import bfs as bfs_validation
16. 
17. 
18. def evaluate_bfs_multisol_batch(
19.     sampler,
20.     predict_fn,
21.     sample_count,
22.     rng_key,
23.     extras,
24.     save_results_fn,
25.     filename="bfs_accuracy",
26. ) -> Dict[str, float]:
27.   """Collect, evaluate, sample, validate and save BFS multi-solution results."""
28.   processed_samples = 0
29.   preds = []
30.   outputs = []
31.   adjacency_batches = []
32.   source_batches = []
33. 
34.   while processed_samples < sample_count:
35.     feedback = next(sampler)
36.     batch_size = feedback.outputs[0].data.shape[0]
37.     outputs.append(feedback.outputs)
38.     new_rng_key, rng_key = jax.random.split(rng_key)
39.     cur_preds, _ = predict_fn(new_rng_key, feedback.features)
40.     preds.append(cur_preds)
41.     processed_samples += batch_size
42.     adjacency_batches.append(feedback[0][0][2].data)
43.     source_batches.append(np.argmax(feedback[0][0][1].data, axis=1))
44. 
45.   outputs = concat_tree(outputs, axis=0)
46.   adjacency = concat_tree(adjacency_batches, axis=0)
47.   source_nodes = concat_tree(source_batches, axis=0)
48.   preds = concat_tree(preds, axis=0)
49.   out = clrs.evaluate(outputs, preds)
50. 
51.   categorical = evaluate_sampling_pair(
52.       model_sample_fn=lambda data: bfs_sampling.sample_bfs_categorical(data),
53.       true_sample_fn=lambda data: bfs_sampling.sample_bfs_categorical(data),
54.       model_input=[preds],
55.       true_input=outputs,
56.       adjacency=adjacency,
57.       source_nodes=source_nodes,
58.       validate_fn=bfs_validation.check_valid_bfs_tree,
59.   )
60.   random_sampling = evaluate_sampling_pair(
61.       model_sample_fn=lambda data: dfs_sampling.sample_random_list(data),
62.       true_sample_fn=lambda data: dfs_sampling.sample_random_list(data),
63.       model_input=[preds],
64.       true_input=outputs,
65.       adjacency=adjacency,
66.       source_nodes=source_nodes,
67.       validate_fn=bfs_validation.check_valid_bfs_tree,
68.   )
69.   prim = evaluate_sampling_pair(
70.       model_sample_fn=lambda data, s: bfs_sampling.sample_bfs_prim(data, s),
71.       true_sample_fn=lambda data, s: bfs_sampling.sample_bfs_prim(data, s),
72.       model_input=[preds],
73.       true_input=outputs,
74.       adjacency=adjacency,
75.       source_nodes=source_nodes,
76.       validate_fn=bfs_validation.check_valid_bfs_tree,
77.       s=source_nodes,
78.   )
79.   beam = evaluate_sampling_pair(
80.       model_sample_fn=lambda data, s: bfs_sampling.sample_bfs_beam(
81.           data, s, beam_width=3),
82.       true_sample_fn=lambda data, s: bfs_sampling.sample_bfs_beam(
83.           data, s, beam_width=3),
84.       model_input=[preds],
85.       true_input=outputs,
86.       adjacency=adjacency,
87.       source_nodes=source_nodes,
88.       validate_fn=bfs_validation.check_valid_bfs_tree,
89.       s=source_nodes,
90.   )
91. 
92.   result_dict = reports.build_bfs_result_dict(
93.       adjacency_flat=[i.flatten() for i in adjacency],
94.       source_nodes=source_nodes,
95.       categorical=categorical,
96.       random_sampling=random_sampling,
97.       prim=prim,
98.       beam=beam,
99.   )
100.   save_results_fn(result_dict, f"{filename}_BFS")
101. 
102.   if extras:
103.     out.update(copy.deepcopy(extras))
104.   return {k: _unpack(v) for k, v in out.items()}
105. 
106. 
107. def _unpack(v):
108.   try:
109.     return v.item()
110.   except (AttributeError, ValueError):
111.     return v
112. 
113.
```
